items.title: One dead, three injured as 30-year-old building collapses in Lafia
items.description: By Edwin Phillip, Lafia LAFIA — Tragedy struck the Tudun Amba area of Lafia, Nasarawa State, after a 30-year-old mud house collapsed on a family of six, killing a four-year-old girl and injuring three others. The incident occurred at about 2am on Thursday, shortly after rainfall. An eyewitness, Kefas Abu Danjuma, who is the deceased girl’s uncle, said the two-room building housed six people from two families. According to him, one room was occupied by his uncle and his three children, while the other housed his brother, his wife and their two children. He said his uncle and his children sustained injuries that were not severe, while his brother’s four-year-old daughter died in the collapse. He added that the family’s two-year-old daughter was also critically injured and had been referred from the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, to the University of Jos Teaching Hospital (JUTH) for further treatment. “The building had six people. The first room was occupied by my uncle and his three children, while the second was occupied by my brother, his wife and two children. “My uncle and his children sustained injuries, but they are not that severe. My brother lost his four-year-old daughter, while his two-year-old daughter is battling for her life,” he said. The deceased child has since been buried, while the other victims remained at the emergency unit of the hospital in Lafia as of the time of filing this report. Danjuma attributed the collapse to the devastating effects of flooding that had affected the area for about 12 years, alleging that there had been no government intervention to address the problem. “We have been suffering from this for about 12 years now. Nobody has come to check how the street is doing. We need the help of government. Without government, we cannot do anything in this situation, especially for those in the hospital and with the building also. It is painful for us as a family, and we leave everything to God,” he said. Also speaking, the youth chairman of Tudun Amba community, Jonathan Ovye Kuje, said residents received a distress call following the collapse. Kuje described the incident as shocking, particularly the death of the child, and prayed for the survival of the two-year-old girl who was referred to JUTH. He warned that similar incidents could occur in the community if urgent measures were not taken to address gully erosion and the deteriorating condition of roads. “People living within the street cannot even have access to their homes because the road is caving in. People are unable to use their motorcycles to get to their houses, and most buildings are being eaten up by erosion. That is one of the factors that contributed to the collapse of this building,” he said. He appealed to the government to intervene by constructing proper drainage channels to control the flow of water and prevent further damage to homes and infrastructure. Efforts to speak with the relevant authorities were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post One dead, three injured as 30-year-old building collapses in Lafia appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: How Karoline Leavitt Debased Her Job
items.description: The lie is the elemental matter of the Trump administration. The value of lying is Donald Trump’s deepest belief. He built his celebrity image through shameless and constant deceit that permitted him to bounce from blunder to blunder while constantly reeling in new suckers. Lying is also what binds his loyalists to him: The highest calling of any figure in Trump world is to refuse any concessions to reality when Trump commands it, and the surest ticket to oblivion is to speak the truth. All of this has made the job of press secretary in a Trump administration less, not more, important than it normally is. In most administrations, the White House press secretary has a unique role in shaping public opinion, whereas the other staffers are concerned principally with governing. In Trump’s White House, distorting reality, rather than trying to improve it, is the highest priority for every official, including and especially the president himself. In an administration where everybody’s main priority is to lie on television, the role of the press secretary is redundant. Karoline Leavitt, who departed as press secretary this week, did the job perfectly well. But the job, as defined by this administration, is not terribly demanding. Traditional press secretaries long engaged in “spin,” a now-antiquated term to describe the delicate art of arranging facts in the most flattering light. Spin requires real skill. Its practitioners must grasp the underlying reality, which points must be danced around and which emphasized, and how to walk a reporter from their skeptical premise to the administration’s desired conclusion. Leavitt never engaged in spin, and she probably wouldn’t know how. Her method of replying to queries relied on the blunt-force repetition of talking points, however unresponsive they might be, sprinkling in heavy doses of personal abuse and slander. [ From the July issue: Use it or lose it ] Consider a sample of her style, plucked somewhat at random. It is the first item on a celebratory list of Leavitt highlights released by the administration—which is to say it is not some unfortunate slip-up but one of her proudest moments. The exchange in question took place on January 15, 2026, between Leavitt and Niall Stanage, the White House columnist for The Hill . Stanage asked Leavitt how to square then–Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem’s statement that the department had done “everything correctly” with the fact that 32 people had died in ICE custody over the past year, 170 U.S. citizens had been detained, and Renee Good was shot and killed. A few lines of defense sprang to my mind as I listened to the question. If my job were to defend the administration, I’d reply that, yes, 32 people died in custody, but that figure says nothing about whether those deaths were caused by ICE. And don’t all police agencies sometimes detain the wrong person in the course of investigating crimes? If ICE is performing somewhat less efficiently than other law-enforcement agencies, maybe it needs more resources for facilities and training. A handful of facts and figures could have reframed this horrific scandal as a one-off failure amid mere business as usual. Leavitt used none of these defenses. She first responded by asking Stanage why he believed Good had been shot. When Stanage replied that he believed an agent had acted recklessly, Leavitt savaged him as biased. “You’re a left-wing hack. You’re not a reporter. You’re posing in this room as a journalist. And it’s so clear by the premise of your question,” she said. “You should be reporting on the facts. You should be reporting on the cases.” [ David A. Graham: A dangerous new attack on press freedom ] Despite attacking Stanage for supposedly failing to report on “the facts,” which his question included, Leavitt’s reply did not cite any numbers at all. “Do you have the numbers of how many American citizens were killed at the hands of illegal aliens, who ICE is trying to remove from this country?” she asked, without producing them herself. In the same exchange, Leavitt complained that Stanage had degraded the august profession of White House reporter: “You and the people in the media who have such biases but fake like you’re a journalist—you shouldn’t even be sitting in that seat.” In reality, Leavitt herself, in one of her first and most important moves as press secretary, invited numerous opinion journalists and influencers to hold permanent seats in the briefing room alongside traditional journalists. So even if it actually were true that Stanage is “biased,” her complaint that this would disqualify him from the job would still have been at odds with her policy. This exchange, in miniature, shows how Leavitt conducted her briefings. Instead of the journalists in the room, her audience was loyalists who require no convincing, and who believe any news story that reflects poorly on Trump is by definition a hoax. Leavitt communicated effectively to this audience because she seemed to be one of them. For this reason, she will be easily replaced by another, equally effective functionary plucked from among the millions of Americans capable of the rudimentary task of responding to questions with repetitive, childish insults. In an administration rife with memorable rogues, Leavitt will fade into obscurity.

items.title: Umahi orders closure of old Niger Bridge for repairs
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — The Minister of Works, Engr. David Umahi, has ordered the temporary closure of the old Niger Bridge for major rehabilitation works. Umahi, who spoke at the Ogbunike interchange linking Anambra State to the Second Niger Bridge, said the closure would take effect seven days from Friday, with traffic diverted to the Second Niger Bridge. He said the closure was necessary to enable the installation of solar-powered streetlights and closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras on the bridge. “Seven days from today (Friday), we are going to close the first Niger Bridge and traffic will be diverted to the second Niger Bridge so that we can install the solar lights and the CCTV. “We will restore the first Niger Bridge to the same quality as the Third Mainland Bridge in Lagos. That is the message and directive of Mr President,” Umahi said. The minister also urged people of the South-East to appreciate the projects being undertaken by President Bola Tinubu’s administration in the region while asking for more development. He expressed concern over what he described as frequent complaints of marginalisation by some content creators in the South-East whenever there was a challenge in the region. Umahi questioned what such critics had to say about previous administrations, which he said did not undertake comparable projects in the region. He urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, arguing that doing so would enable the region to benefit from the continuation of the administration’s projects. “South-East people must vote for the president in 2027. If they are insulting me, it is not my business because they can’t face me face to face. So it makes me happy that I am taking the attention of those insulting me. But the truth remains the truth,” he said. Umahi added: “Vote for President Tinubu so that these dividends of democracy will continue, even in improved form, after the election. “Let it not be that when other people are voting, the people of the South-East will be playing football and tomorrow we will start to complain. It is not acceptable.” The former Ebonyi State governor said the South-East had never witnessed the level of road infrastructure development currently being undertaken under the Tinubu administration. “I was a governor, a deputy governor and party chairman, and never in the history of the South-East did we witness even five per cent of what we are witnessing now. All our roads are being fixed and we are taking them for granted,” he said. Umahi further said the 2027 election would provide an opportunity for the South-East to demonstrate its appreciation for the Federal Government’s interventions in the region. He urged the people to avoid what he described as regional politics, hatred and sentiment, saying political support should be based on mutual interests. “Our votes will not make our brother president and if you are insulting me because of our brother, you are wasting time because we are friends. “I am telling him to support the president because he cannot win. When our time comes, other people will support us. We will not play regional politics and politics of hate and sentiment,” Umahi said. He expressed confidence that Tinubu would win the 2027 presidential election, adding that political forces supporting the President were working together in Anambra State. He also thanked the President for what he described as his administration’s interventions in the South-East, saying the region had regained its pride of place in Nigeria. Umahi further assured contractors handling various Federal Government projects that outstanding certificates generated for completed work would soon be paid. The post Umahi orders closure of old Niger Bridge for repairs appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bolgatanga Girls restores boarding status of student allegedly defiled by watchmen
items.description: Bolgatanga Girls’ Senior High School has restored the boarding status of the student at the centre of an alleged sexual abuse case involving two watchmen at the school. The decision was communicated in a letter dated August 20, 2026, from the Headmistress of the school to the student’s parent. According to the letter, the decision followed a directive from the Ghana Education Service (GES) for the school to reverse the student’s day status and restore her boarding arrangement. The development comes after the Ministry of Education intervened in the matter and directed that the student’s boarding status be restored immediately. The ministry said the student could not be held responsible for the alleged abuse and directed the GES to investigate the incident and ensure that she received the necessary medical care and counselling. The case sparked public concern after allegations emerged that the student, who is reported to be 14 years old, was allegedly sexually abused by two watchmen employed at the school. The alleged incident also raised questions about the school’s handling of the student’s welfare after reports that her boarding status had been changed. The Ministry of Education has described the alleged abuse as unacceptable, stressing that schools have a responsibility to protect the safety, dignity and rights of students, particularly vulnerable children. The GES has since taken steps in relation to the matter, while the broader investigation continues. The restoration of the student’s boarding status marks a significant development in the case, following public criticism and calls for authorities to prioritise the student’s welfare and ensure accountability.

items.title: Dzifa Gomashie is my aunt but Tourism Ministry must be dissolved – Shatta Wale
items.description: Dancehall musician Charles Nii Armah Mensah, popularly known as Shatta Wale, has called for the dissolution of the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, accusing the institution of failing to introduce innovative interventions to support Ghana’s creative industry. The award-winning artiste said he was concerned about what he described as the lack of visible support for musicians, actors and other creatives whose work continues to attract audiences in Ghana and beyond. Speaking in an interview on Accra-based GHOne TV, Shatta Wale questioned the impact of the ministry on the growth and development of the creative sector. “We don’t see any innovative things coming out from that side, and it’s not affecting the industry like we did. You know, actors, musicians. We don’t see anything,” he said on Friday, August 28. Shatta Wale argued that creatives who use their work to promote Ghana internationally deserved stronger institutional backing from the state. According to him, the ministry should be more proactive in identifying talented creatives and supporting projects with the potential to project Ghana to international audiences. He questioned why some artistes and creatives who independently produce work that gains international attention are not approached by the ministry for support. The musician maintained that government institutions responsible for the creative sector must move beyond their traditional roles and develop practical initiatives that directly benefit industry players.

items.title: Élections : la CNDP fixe dix impératifs pour encadrer l’utilisation des données personnelles
items.description: À l’approche des opérations et consultations électorales, la Commission nationale de contrôle de la protection des données à caractère personnel (CNDP) rappelle les principales règles à respecter en matière de collecte, de traitement et d’utilisation des données personnelles. L’instance énonce ainsi dix impératifs destinés aux différents acteurs concernés, allant du respect de la loi 09-08 à l’encadrement de la prospection directe et de l’exploitation des opinions politiques, en passant par le signalement des contenus produits par l’intelligence artificielle. Dans ce cadre, la CNDP souligne en premier lieu la nécessité de se conformer aux dispositions de la loi 09-08 relative à la protection des personnes physiques à l’égard du traitement des données à caractère personnel. Les traitements concernés doivent être notifiés à la CNDP avant leur mise en œuvre, conformément à l’article 12. Les acteurs intervenant dans les opérations électorales sont également tenus de respecter la finalité pour laquelle les données sont collectées ainsi que leur durée de conservation, conformément à l’article 3 de la loi 09-08. Une attention particulière est accordée aux données relatives aux opinions politiques. Leur exploitation ne doit pas intervenir sans le consentement explicite de la personne concernée, conformément à l’article 21, alinéas 1 et 2. La prospection directe constitue également un domaine soumis à des règles précises. Celle-ci ne peut être pratiquée sans le consentement préalable des personnes concernées, conformément à l’article 10. La CNDP insiste sur le signalement des contenus générés par l’IA Dans un contexte marqué par l’essor des outils d’intelligence artificielle, la CNDP inclut également dans ses impératifs l’obligation de signaler tout contenu produit par l’IA. Cette exigence s’appuie, selon le document, sur l’article 447-2 du Code pénal marocain de 2018 ainsi que sur les articles 39, 51 et 53 de la loi organique n°53-25 relative à la Chambre des représentants. La collecte des données à caractère personnel doit, par ailleurs, être effectuée dans le respect des principes de loyauté et de transparence, conformément à l’article 3 de la loi 09-08. Les droits des personnes concernées doivent également être garantis. La CNDP renvoie à cet égard au chapitre II de la loi 09-08, qui couvre les articles 5 à 9. Sous-traitance et transferts de données : les autres exigences La CNDP rappelle également que la sous-traitance des traitements de données doit être encadrée par des contrats conformes aux dispositions de la loi 09-08, notamment ses articles 23 et 25. Les transferts de données à caractère personnel doivent, eux aussi, respecter les dispositions de la législation en vigueur, notamment les articles 15 et 18 ainsi que les dispositions du chapitre V de la loi 09-08, comprenant les articles 43 et 44. Enfin, la CNDP appelle les différents acteurs concernés à respecter les règles relatives à la protection des données à caractère personnel, à coopérer avec les instances compétentes et à assumer leur responsabilité en la matière. À travers ces dix impératifs, la CNDP entend ainsi rappeler les obligations qui s’imposent aux acteurs des opérations et consultations électorales en matière de protection des données personnelles, dans un contexte où les usages numériques et le recours à l’intelligence artificielle occupent une place croissante dans le processus électoral. items.title: 'Profound consequences': Indus Water Treaty must not be weaponised, FM Dar warns India
items.description: WASHINGTON: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday warned that any attempt to deprive Pakistan of waters “rightfully allocated to it” under the Indus Waters Treaty would have “profound consequences for regional peace and security”. The IWT has come under strain since India announced in 2025 that it was placing its treaty obligations in abeyance. The announcement followed an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 tourists — an incident New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without evidence. For its part, Pakistan strongly denied the allegations and called for a neutral investigation. In his virtual address to a Washington seminar on “The Indus Waters Treaty: South Asian Security at the Crossroads”, he declared that Pakistan would strongly safeguard its “legitimate rights and interests” under the treaty and international law. FM Dar said the 1960 agreement remained “valid, binding and fully operative” despite India’s unilateral decision in April 2025 to place it “in abeyance”. “The treaty contains no provision permitting either party to unilaterally suspend or place it in abeyance,” he said, adding that neither country could, “through a unilateral political declaration, extinguish obligations solemnly undertaken under international law.” FM Dar said the issue went beyond the bilateral relationship, arguing that it concerned “the sanctity of treaties” and “confidence in international law”. “If solemn treaty obligations can simply be set aside whenever political relations deteriorate, the very purpose of concluding the treaties is undermined,” he said. He also stressed that geography made cooperation unavoidable, noting that “states cannot alter the direction in which rivers flow”. “That is precisely why rules matter,” FM Dar said, urging the international community to preserve treaty-based water governance in South Asia. The foreign minister further said the treaty had survived wars, military crises, diplomatic breakdowns and prolonged political tensions for more than six decades because both countries had understood that water on which “hundreds of millions of lives depend” was too fundamental to be subjected to fluctuations in political relations. “Today, however, that principle faces its gravest challenge,” he said. FM Dar said Pakistan’s position was clear and consistent and that treaty-based proceedings had continued despite India’s assertion of “abeyance”, reinforcing the principle that “unilateral action cannot displace an agreed legal framework”. Pakistan has pursued arbitration over disputes concerning Indian hydroelectric projects on the Western Rivers, particularly Kishenganga and Ratle. The Court of Arbitration at The Hague has continued proceedings, with earlier rulings addressing its jurisdiction and questions concerning the interpretation and application of the treaty. The treaty allocates the three eastern rivers to India and the three western rivers, including the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, primarily to Pakistan, subject to specified Indian uses. FM Dar said resorting to the Permanent Indus Commission, a neutral expert or a Court of Arbitration “is not an act of confrontation” but “the implementation of the very legal framework to which both countries agreed and are bound”. “Pakistan has consistently sought to resolve differences through dialogue, diplomacy and the mechanisms provided under the Treaty,” he said. He said the dispute was especially serious because Pakistan’s agriculture, food security, energy production, livelihoods and economic development depended heavily on the Indus River system. “The Indus Basin is the lifeline of more than 250 million Pakistanis,” Dar said. “Water security for Pakistan is therefore inseparable from economic security, food security and, ultimately, national security.” Against this backdrop, he warned that unilateral interference with the treaty could affect not only South Asian stability but also create “a dangerous precedent for treaty relations everywhere”. “International agreements derive their value from certainty and predictability,” FM Dar said. “If solemn treaty obligations can simply be set aside whenever political relations deteriorate, the very purpose of concluding the treaties is undermined.” He linked the dispute to climate change, saying Pakistan was already among the world’s most water-stressed countries and faced changing precipitation patterns, glacial retreat, floods, droughts and increasing hydrological variability. “These realities should compel greater and stronger cooperation,” he said, calling for improved data-sharing, sustained technical engagement and greater transparency. “But,” he added, “adaptation cannot mean abandonment of agreed legal rights and obligations”. Dar added that the treaty’s dispute-settlement architecture had been designed precisely to withstand disagreements between the two countries. “The answer to disagreement was therefore built into the Treaty itself: dialogue, technical engagement and lawful dispute resolution,” he said. The foreign minister also emphasised that treaty implementation “was never made contingent upon political convenience”. For Pakistan, he said, the preferred approach remained “law over unilateralism, dialogue over confrontation, and cooperation over coercion”. At the same time, Dar sought to make clear that Islamabad considered its water rights a matter of vital national importance. “Any attempt to deprive Pakistan of the waters rightfully allocated to it under the Indus Waters Treaty would have profound consequences for regional peace and security,” he said. “Pakistan will safeguard its legitimate rights and interests under the treaty and international law.” Dar further stated that the IWT had demonstrated for more than 65 years that Pakistan and India could insulate a vital shared resource from their wider political relationship. “That achievement should not be dismantled. It should be preserved,” he said. He proposed three principles for the way forward: that the treaty be “respected and implemented in letter and spirit”; that all questions, differences and disputes be addressed through its mechanisms; and that Pakistan and India restore and strengthen “technical engagement, transparency and data-sharing”. “These are not unreasonable demands,” Dar said. “They are the requirements of an agreement solemnly concluded by two sovereign states and sustained for more than six decades.” He also invoked Pakistan’s recent diplomatic role in facilitating dialogue during the US-Iran crisis, saying the effort reflected Islamabad’s belief that difficult disputes should ultimately be addressed through “engagement, diplomacy and peaceful settlement”. “Pakistan seeks to be a force for peace and stability, in South Asia and beyond,” he said. Dar concluded by urging that the Indus remains “a source of life, livelihood and civilisation, not a fault line for confrontation”. “Shared waters must never be weaponised,” he said. “They should remain a bridge between nations, governed by law, sustained through cooperation, and protected for generations to come.”

items.title: CNG: Tinubu responding to 2027, not Nigerians’ suffering — ADC
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike African Democratic Congress, ADC, on Friday accused President Bola Tinubu of responding to the 2027 election rather than Nigerians’ suffering, dismissing the Federal Government’s renewed push to expand Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, transportation as a political gimmick coming three years too late. For Nigerians who have spent three years battling soaring transport fares, food prices and shrinking purchasing power, the party said, the sudden urgency to make transportation cheaper is unlikely to pass for genuine concern. In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC said the emergency meeting between Tinubu and state governors on reducing transportation costs was more a reaction to political pressure than a genuine response to hardship. “They left the people to suffer for three years, and now that the election approaches they suddenly realise that they could make transportation cheaper,” Abdullahi said. The party questioned why CNG buses were not rapidly deployed when Nigerians first began paying the heavy price of petrol subsidy removal, arguing that the government could have acted much earlier. The ADC said the timing became even more revealing after its presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, put targeted subsidies and the cost of living at the centre of the national political debate. “Why did it take Atiku’s subsidy plan for this government to suddenly start running helter-skelter and to realise the need to bring down the cost of transportation?” Abdullahi asked. The opposition party maintained that the latest intervention showed the administration had options for cushioning the economic pain all along but chose not to deploy them until its electoral interests came under pressure. “No doubt, if these interventions are possible now, they were possible. The difference is that then, President Tinubu did not think it was necessary to support suffering citizens until now when he needs their votes,” the ADC said. It added that Nigerians could tell the difference between a government responding to their suffering and one responding to the prospect of electoral defeat. “A president who truly cares would not wait for three years and an approaching election before treating the cost of transportation as an emergency,” the party said. The ADC also accused the administration of failing to address insecurity, unemployment and the rising cost of living, saying the 2027 election had exposed the political consequences of those failures. “One thing is clear, President Tinubu is not suddenly responding to the suffering of Nigerians. He is responding to ADC and Atiku; he is responding to the impending reality of the 2027 election,” the party said. items.title: NSMQ 2026: Achimota School retain seeded status, shut out Accra rivals
items.description: ‎It was an all-Accra battle at the Main Auditorium, but Achimota School quickly showed they had no intention of letting their fellow city rivals disrupt their march to the quarter-finals. The two-time champions came into the contest against Accra Girls’ and Accra High School with their seeded status at stake, and from the opening exchanges, they looked the more settled of the three schools. Achimota started strongly and held the lead after the first round, with Accra Girls’ keeping the gap within reach while Accra High School struggled to match the pace. But Round Two gave the champions the opening they needed. They pulled further clear, leaving both Accra Girls’ and Accra High with the difficult task of mounting a comeback against a school that was becoming increasingly comfortable at the top. ‎ ‎The Problem of the Day did little to change the picture. Achimota and Accra Girls’ managed just one correct answer each, while Accra High School drew a blank. With the scores largely unchanged, Achimota returned to the contest still firmly in command, and their consistency began to put real pressure on the two challengers. ‎ ‎Accra Girls’ managed to stay within striking distance for a while, but Achimota held the lead.By the fourth round, the two-time champions had stretched their advantage to a commanding margin, while Accra High School had been left fighting to stay in contention. From there, the contest was increasingly about how much further Achimota could extend their lead rather than who would take first place. ‎ ‎The contest ended with Achimota School scoring 56 points, comfortably ahead of Accra Girls’ 40 and Accra High School’s 28. The result preserves Achimota’s seeded status and sends the two-time champions into the quarter-finals, while the two fellow Accra contenders see their hopes of progressing further come to an end. ‎ ‎The 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz is produced by Primetime Limited and sponsored by the Ghana Education Service with support from Goil Plc, Prudential Life Insurance, Pepsodent, Trustur AI, Cowbell, Jupay Money Transfer, Lumevax, GTP, SpinCITI Laundromat, Didi Jollof, Bel Beverages, Accra College of Medicine and Coronation Insurance and Academic City University The Broadcast on JoyNews is sponsored by: VitaMilk, Entrance University of Health Sciences, Chartered Institute of Management Accountants and NASCO BROADCAST PARTNERS Frutelli, Excellence Publications and Stationery, Didi Shito, Nataraj, Virtual Security Africa, Lef Signature Limited, Sintex Tank, Door Master, New Crystal Hospital, Palm University College, Ayuda, Prospectus Ghana Limited, Family Health University and Myst Water.

items.title: Water supply disrupted in parts of Western Accra after pipeline damage
items.description: Water supply to several communities in Western Accra has been temporarily disrupted following damage to a 500mm-diameter main pipeline supplying the affected areas, Ghana Water Ltd (GWL) has announced. The disruption occurred after excavation works being carried out by AWERCO Construction Ltd for the construction of underground storm drains between Kaneshie First Light and Hansonic Junction damaged the pipeline. According to GWL, the excavation resulted in a burst on the major water line, causing water to flood the entire trench and preventing immediate access to the damaged section. The affected communities include Mallam, Darkuman, Kaneshie, Mataheko, Korle Bu, Mamprobi, Dansoman Township and Chorkor, as well as surrounding areas. GWL said its engineers and technical teams were working continuously to repair the damaged pipeline and restore normal water supply. The immediate challenge, however, is gaining access to the affected section of the line. The company said its teams are currently dewatering the flooded trench to expose the damaged pipeline and enable repair works to proceed. Preparatory work has already begun at one end of the damaged line while dewatering operations continue. The extent of the damage and the time required to complete the repair were not specified in the statement. The 500mm main pipeline is an important supply line serving several densely populated communities in the western part of the capital. The disruption is therefore expected to affect households, businesses and institutions within the affected areas until repairs are completed. GWL urged affected customers to bear with the situation as its technical teams work to restore supplies. Management of Ghana Water Ltd expressed regret over the inconvenience caused by the interruption and assured customers that every effort was being made to restore normal water supply as quickly as possible. The company said it would provide further updates on the progress of the repair works and the restoration of supply through its official communication channels. For residents in the affected communities, the immediate priority remains access to alternative sources of water while GWL works to repair the damaged pipeline and resume normal distribution. GWL said customers should rely on its official channels for updates on the repair and restoration timetable.

items.title: Autopsy shows National Guard fatally shot Memphis man in the back
items.description: A bullet fired by members of the Tennessee National Guard entered the back of 20-year-old Tyrin Johnson, pierced his lung and killed him, an autopsy report shows, contradicting the initial account given by officials. Authorities previously said that Johnson was shot by two guard members in the chest on 5 July in Memphis, after he faced them with a gun. A copy of the autopsy seen by the BBC said that a single bullet penetrated his back on the right side before exiting through his upper right chest. Johnson’s family is calling for accountability following the release of the autopsy report. The National Guard did not immediately respond to the BBC’s request for comment. “Be transparent – you shot him in the back,” Evaniel Johnson, the slain 20-year-old’s grandfather, told the Associated Press. “I just want to make sure somebody be responsible for what happened. Some accountability. They ain’t never going to bring my grandson back. “If he ain’t caused you no threat, you know what I’m saying, you have no reason to be killing,” Johnson, a former Nashville correctional officer, added. The autopsy was conducted by the West Tennessee Regional Forensic Center Office of the Medical Examiner. Its report included the “investigative narrative” of an agent with the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation who said Memphis police and National Guard troops were first called to scene after reports of nearby gunfire. They encountered Johnson, the investigative narrative said, who then “grabbed at his waistband”. “Law enforcement officers saw the unknown male draw a firearm,” according to the officer’s account of events, included in the report. “Law enforcement officers then shot at the unknown male, striking him once in the chest.” Separate from the officer’s account, the report also said Johnson was carrying a “handgun magazine with rounds”. In Tennessee, gun laws allow legal gun owners to openly carry weapons. “The autopsy findings reinforce the serious concerns we have regarding Tyrin’s shooting and the circumstances surrounding his encounter with the Memphis Safe Task Force,” the Johnson family’s lawyer Andre Wharton, who shared the autopsy report with the BBC, said in a statement. “The fact that Tyrin was actually shot in the back, contrasted with officer and task force’s accounts, only further underscores the devastating nature of this encounter.” Johnson’s cause of death was listed as “homicide”, the official term used when a death is caused by another person. The term does not always include intent, and no criminal charges have been filed to date. Asked by the BBC about the conflicting findings, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation referred to its original July statement, saying the investigation remained “active and ongoing”. “Reports that Tyrin Johnson turned and pointed a gun at National Guardsmen were not distributed by the TBI,” the agency said. Tennessee State Representative Justin Pearson released a statement on X on Friday saying “Johnson should be alive today” and called for an investigation. “The National Guard is not welcome here,” he continued. “Mr Johnson’s murder is a horrifying example of the brutality and injustice the Memphis Unsafe Task Force has brought to our city.” The troops were in Memphis as part of the Memphis Safe Task Force, created by US President Donald Trump amid a larger effort to deploy National Guard troops to US cities. Trump has said the troops deployment – largely in Democrat-led cities, including Chicago, Los Angeles and Washington DC – was meant to combat crime.

items.title: Burkina : Le Commissaire principal Issa Zongo prend la tête du GSIPN
items.description: Le Commissaire principal de police Issa Zongo a officiellement pris le commandement du Groupe spécial d’intervention de la Police nationale (GSIPN), ce jeudi 27 août 2026, à Badnoogo. Il a reçu le drapeau national des mains du Directeur général de la police nationale, Thierry Dofizouho Tuina, qui présidait la cérémonie. Nommé à ce poste lors du Conseil des ministres du 18 juin 2026, il succède ainsi à la tête de cette unité d’élite. Dans sa prise de parole, le nouveau commandant a affirmé placer son mandat sous le signe de l’engagement, du professionnalisme et de la continuité. Pour lui, cette nomination constitue avant tout une responsabilité confiée par les autorités. « C’est donc un sentiment de joie et de fierté qui nous anime ce jour », a-t-il déclaré, avant de souligner que les résultats obtenus lors des opérations précédentes ont renforcé la confiance des autorités envers son équipe. « Cette bataille va donc se poursuivre, car la lutte contre l’insécurité est loin d’être gagnée », a-t-il averti. Afin de faire face aux défis à venir, Issa Zongo entend renforcer les capacités opérationnelles de son unité et intensifier les missions sur le terrain. « Nous allons nous affûter, renforcer nos capacités et reprendre le combat pour aller davantage de l’avant », a-t-il assuré. Le commandant a par ailleurs rappelé que la mission du GSIPN ne constitue pas une nouveauté pour lui et ses hommes, l’unité ayant déjà été engagée dans plusieurs zones du Burkina Faso. « On ne change pas une équipe qui gagne », a-t-il martelé, mettant en avant la solidité et l’expérience du groupe. La nouvelle tenue de cette Unité Insistant sur les qualités requises au sein de cette unité d’intervention, le Commissaire principal Zongo a évoqué la force mentale, l’engagement et le professionnalisme. Il s’est dit confiant quant aux missions à venir, estimant que le personnel du GSIPN est déjà aguerri aux réalités opérationnelles, aussi bien en milieu urbain qu’en milieu rural. Créé en novembre 2023 en remplacement de l’Unité d’intervention polyvalente de la police nationale (UIP-PN), le GSIPN est chargé de gérer les situations de crise sécuritaire complexes et les opérations d’intérêt stratégique. Sidziguin Irène Corinne SAWADOGO (Stagiaire) Minute.bf

items.title: Tinubu approves comprehensive forensic audit of IPPIS, federal agencies, ministries
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has directed the Minister of Finance and Co-ordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, to oversee and coordinate a comprehensive forensic audit of Federal Government systems. The audit will include a review of the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System (IPPIS), Federal Government agencies, and their administration and internal controls. President Tinubu’s directive follows the Federal Executive Council’s resolution on August 19, 2026, in response to findings by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) on “fake agencies”, ghost workers, and other control failures. The exercise will establish the nature and extent of weaknesses in Government’s control system, and determine how such weaknesses have been exploited. A statement by Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, stated that the review will comprise two interconnected components. According to the statement, the first will focus on a forensic audit of Government systems, particularly IPPIS and related payroll, personnel, pension and financial-management platforms. “It will examine reported cases of ghost workers and payroll fraud, reconcile the figures identified by the ICPC, trace how fictitious or ineligible persons were enrolled, and review access, identity, biometric and bank-account controls,” it stated. “The exercise will also examine the interfaces between IPPIS and other government platforms, including GIFMIS, Remita, the Treasury Single Account (TSA) and Sub-TSA, to determine whether fraud resulted from system defects, process failures, inadequate segregation of duties or deliberate circumvention.” It explained that the second component of the audit will cover all Federal Government agencies, departments, commissions, councils, parastatals and other government bodies. ” It will establish a definitive inventory of such bodies and verify their legal basis, while examining how entities obtain official recognition, budgetary consideration, correspondence privileges, office facilities and access to government systems,” it said. It further stated that the exercise will assess governance, procurement, internal-audit, and oversight controls across Government to close systemic weaknesses that could allow irregular entities or persons to access public resources. “President Tinubu directed that the exercise be conducted with the highest standards of independence, professionalism and forensic integrity. “The audit team will have access to relevant government systems and records. It will collaborate with the ICPC to ensure that the review complements all ongoing investigations, prosecutions and recoveries.” The statement ssid President Tinubu expects the exercise to go beyond identifying individual cases of fraud or administrative failure by strengthening the architecture of Government, closing systemic loopholes, improving data verification and reconciliation, reinforcing accountability, and ensuring that only duly constituted entities and eligible personnel have access to Government resources. “The exercise underscores the President’s commitment to strengthening transparency, accountability, fiscal governance and institutional integrity across the Federal Government,” it concluded. items.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs0.58, HSD by Rs0.17
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs0.58 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.17 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs342.02 per litre while HSD will cost Rs371.44 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to a Petroleum Division notification, the new prices will be applicable from Aug 29 to Aug 31. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Keta Municipal Hospital marks 100 years of continuous healthcare service
items.description: Keta Municipal Hospital in the Volta Region is set to mark 100 years of continuous healthcare service to residents of Keta and surrounding communities. The Ghana Health Service facility, located in the Keta Municipality, will celebrate its centenary in October 2026, marking a century of service to the people and a significant milestone in the history of healthcare delivery in the area. The anniversary is expected to provide an opportunity to reflect on the hospital’s contribution to healthcare over the past century, while highlighting its current capabilities, challenges and plans for the future. The centenary activities, which began in July, will run through October and are expected to bring together healthcare professionals, stakeholders, sister health institutions, community members and other partners. Among the activities planned are a scientific lecture, an inter-hospital fun games event, a medical screening exercise and a community clean-up exercise. The activities will culminate in a main event week and the anniversary climax in October. Beyond celebrating its history, the hospital intends to use the centenary to draw attention to its present-day operations and the needs required to improve healthcare delivery. The anniversary will highlight the hospital’s service offerings, staff welfare concerns and the need for equipment retooling to enable the facility to respond effectively to the healthcare needs of the municipality and surrounding communities. The centenary planning committee said the celebration is also intended to create greater public awareness of the hospital’s role and encourage broader engagement with stakeholders on its future direction. The milestone comes as the hospital reflects on a century in which its role in the health needs of Keta and neighbouring communities has continued to evolve alongside Ghana’s healthcare system. The organisers are therefore seeking to use the centenary as more than a commemoration of the past, but also as a platform to discuss how the hospital can be strengthened to meet the healthcare needs of future generations.

items.title: Le Roi adresse un message de condoléances à la famille de feu Abdelaziz Bennani
items.description: Le Roi Mohammed VI a adressé un message de condoléances aux membres de la famille du militant et figure de la défense des droits de l'homme, feu Abdelaziz Bennani. Dans ce message, le Souverain exprime aux membres de la famille du défunt et à tous ses proches, et à travers eux, à l'ensemble de la famille des droits de l'homme, Ses vives condoléances et Sa sincère compassion, à la suite de la perte de l'une des figures du militantisme en faveur des droits de l'homme au Maroc, dans les pays arabes et le monde, implorant le Tout Puissant d'agréer le défunt en Sa sainte miséricorde et d'accorder aux membres de sa famille patience et consolation. Le message Royal souligne les qualités du défunt, son héritage et son engagement et militantisme en faveur des droits de l'homme, à travers les différentes missions et responsabilités qu'il a assumées, notamment sa contribution significative dans le cadre de l'Instance Équité et Réconciliation et sa présidence d'une organisation nationale de défense des droits de l'homme, ainsi que ses rôles pionniers au sein de plusieurs organisations et réseaux arabes et internationaux de défense des droits de l'homme. Le Souverain évoque, en outre, les nobles qualités humaines dont le défunt a fait preuve tout au long de sa vie, riche d’engagement et de dévouement, ainsi que ses contributions actives reconnues, tant au niveau national qu’international, en faveur de la protection et de la consolidation des droits de l’homme et de leurs valeurs universelles, ainsi que celles de la justice et de la démocratie, saluant l'attachement indéfectible du défunt aux constantes nationales sacrées et son incarnation d'un patriotisme sincère. Le Roi dit partager les sentiments de la famille de feu Abdelaziz Bennani en cette douloureuse épreuve, la volonté divine étant imparable, implorant le Très Haut de lui accorder patience et réconfort, et d'entourer le défunt de Sa sainte miséricorde et de Sa mansuétude et de l'accueillir en Son vaste paradis. The post Le Roi adresse un message de condoléances à la famille de feu Abdelaziz Bennani appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes : Des journalistes burkinabè saluent les exploits de l’industrie robotique chinoise
items.description: La 2e édition des Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes se déroule du 22 au 26 août 2026 à Beijing, la capitale chinoise. Plus 2 056 robots humanoïdes de 666 équipes issues de 16 pays s'affrontent dans plusieurs disciplines sportives comme le tennis de table, la boxe, des courses, le football, le saut à la corde ou encore l'haltérophilie. Cette compétition met en lumière les progrès impressionnants réalisés par les entreprises chinoises spécialisées dans la robotique, ainsi que la place prépondérante occupée par la Chine en matière d'innovation dans le secteur. Rien que pour le premier semestre de 2026, le pays a exporté plus de 40 mille robots humanoïdes , portant sa part des livraisons mondiales à 97 %. Des hommes de médias du Burkina Faso, présents en Chine, ont livré leurs impressions sur le développement de la robotique chinoise. De l'avis de Souleymane Diallo, directeur de communication au Service d'information du gouvernement, les jeux mondiaux en cours montrent que la robotique est en train de franchir une étape décisive. « Voir des robots pratiquer des disciplines sportives et battre les records de nos meilleurs sportifs, c'est une autre dimension. Elle va au-delà de l'industrie et des services », a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, l'avenir des robots humanoïdes sera marqué par une complémentarité croissante entre l'homme et la machine. « Les robots pourront prendre en charge des tâches répétitives, pénibles ou dangereuses, tandis que l'humain conservera sa capacité de décision, de créativité et d’empathie. Cette évolution va profondément transformer notre manière de travailler, de produire et de vivre », a indiqué M. Diallo. Pour lui, l'ère de la robotique ouvre d'immenses opportunités, notamment pour les pays africains, à condition que l'on puisse développer les compétences, la formation et les cadres éthiques nécessaires. « Pour moi, l'enjeu ne devrait donc pas être de chercher à remplacer l'homme par le robot, mais de faire de la technologie un levier au service du progrès humain et du développement. Et, ces Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes me questionnent sur l'intérêt d'orienter cette technologie vers la pratique des sports de compétition », s'est-il interrogé. « Complémentarité intelligente » Pour sa part, Sié Simplice Hien, rédacteur en chef de l'hebdomadaire Sidwaya Sport, a soutenu que le développement spectaculaire des robots humanoïdes en Chine ces dernières années marque un tournant majeur dans l'histoire de la technologie. « La tenue de la 2e édition des jeux mondiaux de robots humanoïdes illustre parfaitement cette évolution et le fait que nous ne sommes plus dans une simple démonstration technologique, mais dans une phase où les robots commencent à interagir avec le monde réel, à accomplir des tâches complexes et même à accomplir des activités sportives telles que le football, la boxe, l'athlétisme, etc. », a-t-il commenté. Dans cette évolution fulgurante, M. Hien a relevé que ce qui est particulièrement remarquable, c'est le passage progressif de la robotique industrielle à des applications beaucoup plus proches de la vie quotidienne. « La capacité des robots humanoïdes à reproduire certains mouvements et comportements humains ouvre des perspectives considérables. Pour moi la robotique deviendra à l'avenir progressivement un partenaire de l'homme plutôt qu'un simple outil. Elle pourrait par exemple contribuer à effectuer des travaux répétitifs et pénibles afin d'améliorer la productivité », a expliqué le journaliste burkinabè. La robotique, a-t-il poursuivi, façonnera l'avenir, mais l'enjeu ne sera pas de remplacer l'homme par la machine. « Il sera plutôt question de construire une complémentarité intelligente entre l'intelligence humaine et celle artificielle afin que le progrès technologique demeure au service du développement et du bien-être de l'humanité », a argué Sié Simplice Hien. De son côté, Kowoma Marc Doh, conseiller en communication, a affirmé que la robotique va révolutionner le monde en termes de développement industriel et économique. « En effet, les robots constituent une main-d'œuvre qualifiée, capable de réaliser en un temps record le travail de plusieurs compétences humaines réunies, surtout dans le domaine industriel. Dans ce cas, les entreprises économisent en termes de recrutement massif de personnes. » Toutefois, il s'inquiète que des compétences humaines se retrouvent au chômage au regard des performances que réalisent les robots humanoïdes. Pour M. Doh, la robotique pourrait être utile dans les secteurs agricole et minier en Afrique. « L'Afrique possède un potentiel agricole en termes de terres arables, mais les moyens de production à grande échelle font défaut. La robotique peut aider à la fabrication des machines agricoles et booster la production. En ce qui concerne le secteur minier, la robotique peut servir également à la fabrication des matériaux facilitant l'exploitation minière. En somme, la robotique dans ces secteurs peut contribuer fortement à la croissance économique et à l'autosuffisance alimentaire en Afrique », a-t-il souligné. Karim BADOLO CGTN Français

items.title: Four-wicket Robinson stars as Pakistan collapse in second Test
items.description: Ollie Robinson took a sensational 4-11 in 13 overs as Pakistan collapsed to 110 all out in the second Test against England at Lord’s on Friday. But on a day when 13 wickets fell in total, England then slumped to 13-2 in their second innings on a pitch still offering significant seam movement. England, however, had recovered to 81-3 — an overall lead of 261 runs — when bad light forced an early close to the second day. The hosts are seeking an unassailable 2-0 lead in a three-match series. Robinson was well-supported by fast bowler Jofra Archer, who did the initial damage in a return of 3-26, and fellow paceman Josh Tongue, who finished with 2-27 after making a Test-best 30 not out at number 11 earlier on Friday. England’s Ollie Robinson (2L) celebrates with teammates after taking the wicket of Pakistan’s Khurram Shahzad on day two of the second Test match between England and Pakistan at Lord’s cricket ground in Leeds, London on August 28, 2026. Opener Azan Awais top-scored for the tourists with a determined 46, after he was dropped on eight in the slips by Harry Brook. Saud Shakeel’s 16 was the only other double-figure contribution by a Pakistan batsman. An innings lasting a mere 37.2 overs ended with Pakistan nine wickets down after opener Imam-ul-Haq was unable to bat following a calf injury suffered when fielding on Thursday. Gus Atkinson (45) and Tongue had earlier frustrated Pakistan with a tenth-wicket partnership of 47. Archer made the breakthrough when a flat-footed Shan Masood, opening in place of Imam, edged a 146 kilometre per hour full-length delivery to wicket-keeper Jamie Smith for one. Tongue then struck with what became the last ball before lunch when Abdullah Shafique was caught behind to leave Pakistan 16-2. Azam falls cheaply on return Pakistan captain Babar Azam got off the mark in style as he belted an 88 mph Tongue delivery through the covers for four before a flashing drive off Atkinson also sped to the boundary. That was as good as it got for Azam, who missed Pakistan’s crushing innings and 103-run defeat in the first Test at Headingley last week with a finger injury, before he nicked Tongue to a diving Jordan Cox at third slip. England’s Jordan Cox (2L) holds on to a catch to dismiss Pakistan’s Babar Azam on day two of the second Test match between England and Pakistan at Lord’s cricket ground in Leeds, London on August 28, 2026. — AFP Pakistan were 30-3, having been dismissed for 171 and 135 at Headingley. Both Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan were lbw to Robinson before Ali Usman played on to Archer. Pakistan then lost a flurry of wickets, Archer ending the innings in emphatic fashion when he knocked over Mohammad Abbas’s off-stump. Khurram Shahzad gave Pakistan a glimmer of hope with 2-5 in two overs after Ben Duckett (one) mistimed a half-volley to mid-off before Cox (11) was lbw on review. England captain Joe Root, not for the first time in his long career, came in with his side in trouble, at 13-2. Together with Emilio Gay, he kept Pakistan at bay until, on 24, he was plumb lbw to a nip-back ball from Mohammad Ali — the ninth time in 12 Test innings the England great had been leg before wicket. Next ball Brook was also given out lbw to Ali, but the batsman’s review revealed a huge inside edge. England’s Gus Atkinson plays a shot to be caught out for 45 runs on day two of the second Test match between England and Pakistan at Lord’s cricket ground in Leeds, London on August 28, 2026. — AFP In the morning, England resumed on 248-9 after fifties from Smith and Cox helped them recover from a top-order collapse caused by veteran seamer Abbas’s superb burst of 3-4 in 16 balls after Pakistan won the toss. Atkinson was 34 not out and Tongue unbeaten on one. Tongue expertly glanced Ali for four and drilled Abbas through the covers for another boundary, with England’s last-wicket duo largely untroubled by a Pakistan seam attack lacking raw speed. Azam belatedly turned to left-arm spinner Ali Usman. Atkinson, who has a Test century at Lord’s to his credit, drove Usman’s third ball Friday for four but holed out off the next.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Lancement de l’opération de mise à disposition de 15 000 tonnes de céréales aux Provandiers
items.description: Bobo-Dioulasso : Lancement de l’opération de mise à disposition de 15 000 tonnes de céréales aux Provandiers Bobo-Dioulasso, 28 août 2026 – Le ministre délégué auprès du ministre d'État, ministre de l’Agriculture, de l'eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques Amadou Dicko a lancé jeudi, l’opération de mise à disposition de céréales à prix subventionné au profit des Provandiers, afin de réduire le coût de production des aliments pour bétail et volaille et de renforcer la disponibilité des produits aviaires sur le marché national. Selon le directeur général des productions animales, Émilien Bakoné, cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’Offensive agro-pastorale, hydraulique et halieutique 2026-2028, qui fait suite à la première phase mise en œuvre de 2023 à 2025. Elle vise notamment à répondre à la problématique de l’alimentation du bétail, considérée comme une préoccupation majeure pour le secteur de l’élevage. Pour cette première phase, 15 000 tonnes de céréales seront mobilisées. Il s’agit notamment de maïs, de niébé, de sorgho et de mil. À terme, le volume pourrait atteindre 30 000 tonnes, a précisé le directeur général des productions animales. Ces céréales doivent permettre aux Provandiers, spécialisés dans la fabrication d’aliments pour animaux, de produire à moindre coût et, par conséquent, de proposer des aliments accessibles aux éleveurs. Le directeur général de la SONAGESS Wendpagnagdé Alfred Kola a expliqué que les céréales proviennent notamment de l’opération de collecte hors-champ menée auprès des producteurs. Cette collecte a permis à la société de constituer d’importants stocks destinés à accompagner les politiques publiques tout en garantissant un prix rémunérateur aux producteurs. Le DG de la SONAGESS a également insisté sur la destination exclusive de ces céréales. Les stocks mis à la disposition des Provandiers sont strictement destinés à la production d’aliments pour bétail et volaille. Leur utilisation pour la consommation humaine ou à des fins spéculatives est interdite. Des mesures de contrôle devraient être prises afin de prévenir tout détournement de cette opération. Du côté des bénéficiaires, la mesure est accueillie favorablement. Le représentant des Provandiers, Manéré Wilfried Ouédraogo, estime que cette dotation, subventionnée à plus de 50 %, constitue un véritable soulagement pour les acteurs. Elle devrait leur permettre d’améliorer la qualité de leurs productions tout en maîtrisant les coûts. Selon lui, cette initiative répond également à une préoccupation exprimée face à la hausse du prix du maïs sur le marché. Organisés en coopératives et associations, ils ont saisi le ministère de l’Agriculture, qui les a ensuite orientés vers la SONAGESS pour accéder aux stocks mobilisés par l’État. À travers cette opération, les autorités entendent ainsi réduire le coût de l’alimentation animale, soutenir les éleveurs et accroître la disponibilité des produits avicoles sur le marché national, conformément aux objectifs de l’Offensive agro-pastorale, hydraulique et halieutique 2026-2028. Agence d’information du Burkina OSAR/wis

items.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 579, nearly 2,000 still missing: disaster authority
items.description: Nepal’s disaster authority on Friday put the number of people missing after devastating floods at 1,924, two days after the disaster killed at least 579 people in the country. The number of missing includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the rivers where a wall of water powered down on Wednesday morning, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Rescue teams used heavy machinery to dig through mud and debris in Nepalese towns devastated by a flash flood two days ago, as hopes of finding survivors faded and officials worked to reduce the risk of further catastrophic flooding. The flood ripped through villages and valleys, destroying power stations, roads and bridges along a route that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Tibet and is popular with trekkers and pilgrims. Authorities in Nepal used helicopters to search for survivors and drop emergency supplies to thousands cut off in towns and valleys while emergency services, some using sniffer dogs, recovered dozens of bodies swept down into the plains. Around 320 Indian nationals are still missing in the aftermath of the devastating flash flood, a spokesperson for India’s foreign ministry said, adding that at least 400 were stranded but safe on the Chinese side, while another 96 had crossed into Nepal by land. Rescuer help women to move through a muddy road following flash floods and a mudslide in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal on August 28, 2026. —Reuters Dibga Tamang was among the last people rescued from the hard-hit town of Rasuwa on Thursday, airlifted along with three others to an army camp in Nuwakot. “All of our people have gone. They are dead,” Tamang said. “I have no one left waiting for me. Everything and everyone is gone. The end.” The sheer amount of water and debris stirred up now risks triggering a further disaster. Nepal’s disaster management authority warned that a lake formed by debris blocking the Bhotekoshi River was rising and at risk of bursting, while on the other side of the border China said that some three million cubic metres of water, the equivalent of about 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools, was expected to flow into an already dammed lake over the next three days. There is a high risk the lake could breach, with peak flow expected around September 1, Chinese state media said, citing the water resources ministry. Chinese authorities have mobilised an eight-member engineering team to conduct aerial surveys and 3D modelling of the barrier lake, but accessing it was challenging. “After the glacier collapse created the lake, many isolated cliffs and steep cliffs appeared along it,” one of the engineers, Chen Hanxiao, told CCTV. Chen said the general approach to reducing the lake’s threat is to excavate a drainage channel at a lower point of the dam, but the width and depth of that channel needed calculations based on how fast the water will flow and how quickly the lake will fill. Their next tasks were to monitor the lake and collect data from the lake floor, as well as weather monitoring in the coming days. Nepali Army working to rescue 100 trapped in hydropower tunnel Nepali Army teams searched for more than 100 people trapped inside a hydropower tunnel, as India offered to send a specialised rescue team. India has extensive experience with difficult Himalayan tunnel rescues, including specialised teams of “rat-hole” miners. However, the uncertainty was agonising for families waiting for news. “I have not heard from him since I spoke to him at 7am that day. We have not had any news about them either, if they are being rescued or not,” Sita Adhikari, whose husband was trapped in the hydropower tunnel, told reporters. “We will have hope as long as we have our breath… We need them to be rescued as soon as possible,” she said. Nepali Army helicopters carrying bodies of deceased flood victims land at Trishuli camp in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 28, 2026. — AFP Two army helicopters were sent to the Trishuli 3A hydropower project in the mountainous Rasuwa district. “Our focus is on search and rescue of people… some people are trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project,” Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP . “Two helicopters have been dispatched, but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel.” Chinese rescuers reach main site of deadly mudslide Chinese rescuers faced treacherous conditions as they reached the main area wiped out by a deadly mudslide at the Tibet-Nepal border to search for hundreds of missing people, state media reported. Two days after Tibet’s border trade hub of Gyirong was pummelled by a wall of mud and debris, a team of 21 rescuers became the first to reach it in the late afternoon on Friday, state news agency Xinhua said. Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired a meeting of top leaders about rescue operations, as the death toll in Tibet rose to five, with 558 still missing. “There are still many hidden dangers of glaciers, ice lakes and geological disasters in the surrounding area, and rescue is facing great difficulties,” Xinhua reported the leaders as saying. After the mudslide hit on Wednesday, a huge lake formed upstream, raising concerns that it could burst and cause further severe flooding. But risks from that lake are “gradually decreasing”, Chinese state media reported on Friday, adding that rescue operations were “proceeding in an orderly manner”. An excavator in action as rescue workers repair a road leading to Gyirong Port after a mudslide, in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Tibet Autonomous Region, China on August 28, 2026. —Reuters Authorities had earlier paused operations in the worst affected area, citing the risk of renewed flooding due to the lake water beginning to overflow, state broadcaster CCTV said. Later, a CCTV report said water from the lake was “flowing out naturally, with the outflow discharge exceeding the inflow discharge”. “Compared to the high water level in the early morning on August 27, the lake’s water level has dropped by around 10 metres (33 feet), and the risk is gradually decreasing,” it added. It was not immediately clear if the lake was the same as a debris dam that Nepalese authorities warned had burst on Friday. Family members of the missing were being housed in the area by authorities as they waited for news, one woman told AFP . She said she had not been able to reach her relative, a police officer at Gyirong, or his wife, since the disaster happened, and had been told he was missing by his work unit. CCTV said that 499 Chinese nationals and 555 foreigners had been transported out of the disaster zone as of Friday. Rescue workers are using drone-based 3D modelling and thermal imaging detection, as well as manual searches, to locate those still missing, said CCTV . Xi offered Beijing’s help in Nepal’s rescue operations, in a condolence message to the country’s president. “China is willing to actively assist Nepal in its rescue efforts and provide support and aid to the best of its ability,” Xi said according to CCTV . Buildings ‘wiped out like toothpicks’ Around the world, relatives of those missing were desperate for information about their whereabouts. Sneha Sudhir was one of 10 women whose husbands had set out from Nepal on a trek to Tibet’s Mount Kailash when the region was struck by disaster. The men, all from northern Virginia, are among dozens of Americans missing. “Where are they?” Sudhir said tearfully from her home in Chantilly, Virginia, on Thursday. Sudhir said the women were supporting each other and reaching out to officials, politicians and friends and family in the United States and India, hoping for word. “Everybody is taking turns in shedding their tears, wiping it off and getting back to work,” she said. US President Donald Trump said America had offered support to Nepal. Rescued residents react as they meet family members at an army camp following flash floods, in Battar Bazar town of Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 28, 2026. —AFP “Nobody’s ever seen anything quite like that, where very powerful, strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks. It’s a terrible thing. We are sending aid and we’ve spoken to the leadership and we let them know anything they want, they’ll have.” Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also offered “whatever possible assistance was required” in a phone call with his Nepali counterpart, Balendra Shah, according to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). He conveyed to Shah that Pakistan was dispatching emergency relief assistance to Nepal in order to help with the relief efforts, the statement said, as well as expressing condolences and “complete solidarity” with the Nepali leadership and people. Ganesh Aryal, the administrator of Chitwan district, said authorities had recovered 103 bodies from the river system in his district, which is about 100 kilometres away in the plains from the worst-hit region of Trishuli. With local hospitals unable to accommodate all the bodies, district authorities were setting up tents and making arrangements for families to claim their dead relatives, he said. Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who visited flood-hit Nuwakot on Thursday, said the situation was still difficult. “All the state agencies are operating at full capacity. Our first priority now is to save the life of each citizen, search and rescue of the missing, treat the injured and provide immediate relief to the affected families,” he said. The disaster is a major challenge for Shah’s five-month-old government but officials said the country had systems and officials who have experience in handling such tragedies, including the 2015 earthquake that killed nearly 9,000 people. Additional input from AFP

items.description: Azzedine Ounahi s’est rendu à Amsterdam pour discuter avec les dirigeants de l’Ajax, alors que le club néerlandais souhaite toujours renforcer son milieu de terrain. Une rencontre qui ne garantit toutefois pas encore son arrivée aux Pays-Bas. Selon les informations de Foot Mercato, le milieu marocain est actuellement à Amsterdam pour des discussions avec Jordi Cruijff autour d’un éventuel transfert à l’Ajax. La piste est suivie depuis plusieurs semaines par le club amstellodamois, notamment à la demande de son entraîneur Míchel. Le technicien espagnol connaît bien Ounahi pour l’avoir dirigé à Gérone, où les deux hommes ont travaillé ensemble durant une saison. Ounahi, qui compte 55 sélections avec le Maroc, ne correspond toutefois pas exactement au profil de milieu défensif recherché en priorité par l’Ajax. La situation pourrait évoluer en fonction des éventuels départs dans l’entrejeu du club néerlandais. Le joueur reste également courtisé par d’autres formations européennes. Sa valeur est actuellement estimée à 18 millions d’euros par Transfermarkt, même si le montant d’un éventuel transfert reste encore à déterminer. The post Azzedine Ounahi à Amsterdam pour négocier avec l’Ajax appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
