items.title: Ebola en RDC: l’ONU lance un appel urgent pour 1,1 milliard de dollars
items.description: Face à la progression préoccupante de l’épidémie d’Ebola dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), le secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres, a appelé, le jeudi 27 août 2026, la communauté internationale à débloquer d’urgence 1,1 milliard de dollars supplémentaires pour renforcer la riposte. Les Nations unies tirent une nouvelle fois la sonnette d’alarme sur la situation sanitaire dans l’est de la RDC. António Guterres a demandé jeudi un financement additionnel de 1,1 milliard de dollars afin de permettre aux équipes engagées sur le terrain de faire face à l’ampleur croissante de l’épidémie d’Ebola. Le plan d’intervention des Nations unies est estimé à 2,13 milliards de dollars. Mais à ce jour, seuls 48 % de cette enveloppe ont été réunis, selon le secrétaire général de l’ONU. Une part importante des financements déjà disponibles provient notamment d’une contribution conséquente des États-Unis. António Guterres appelle ainsi les donateurs à accélérer leurs efforts. «Sans financement supplémentaire, les opérations vitales se retrouveront à court de fonds au moment même où elles devront s’intensifier», a-t-il averti, déplorant que l’attention accordée par la communauté internationale et les ressources consacrées à la crise demeurent en deçà des besoins. Une progression inquiétante du virus La riposte se déroule dans des conditions particulièrement complexes. Dans l’est du pays, l’insécurité persistante, les déplacements de populations, une grève des agents de santé et les importants mouvements de personnes compliquent considérablement le suivi des cas et les opérations de contrôle de la maladie. Selon l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS), la situation demeure extrêmement préoccupante et pourrait voir l’épidémie actuelle prendre une ampleur supérieure à celle qui avait frappé l’Afrique de l’Ouest entre 2014 et 2016, causant plus de 11 000 décès. Déclarée officiellement à la mi-mai, l’épidémie aurait commencé à circuler dès février, d’après les autorités congolaises. Depuis, sa progression s’est accélérée. Le virus, qui était initialement détecté dans trois zones sanitaires, circule désormais dans près de 60. Autre source d’inquiétude pour les autorités sanitaires: de nombreux cas et décès sont aujourd’hui identifiés directement au sein des communautés, en dehors des chaînes de contacts déjà recensées et placées sous surveillance. Une souche sans vaccin ni traitement homologué La situation est d’autant plus préoccupante que l’épidémie est provoquée par le virus Ebola de type Bundibugyo. À ce stade, aucun vaccin ni traitement n’est officiellement approuvé contre cette souche. Des essais cliniques ont toutefois été lancés dans la région sur plusieurs candidats vaccins et traitements expérimentaux. L’objectif est de déterminer leur efficacité et de disposer de moyens supplémentaires pour contenir la propagation du virus. Parallèlement, les autorités congolaises ont adopté diverses mesures destinées à limiter les contaminations. Elles comprennent notamment la réduction des rassemblements publics, l’application de mesures de distanciation sociale, ainsi que des restrictions concernant les transports et la fermeture de certains aéroports. Ces dispositions pèsent lourdement sur le quotidien des populations des six provinces affectées. L’Ituri figure parmi les zones les plus préoccupantes, dans une région déjà fragilisée par les violences et les attaques de groupes rebelles. L’urgence d’un financement renforcé Pour les Nations unies, le renforcement des ressources financières ne peut plus attendre. Les fonds supplémentaires doivent notamment permettre de maintenir la surveillance épidémiologique, la prise en charge des malades, la prévention des contaminations et les opérations de vaccination. Alors que le virus poursuit sa progression dans un environnement marqué par l’insécurité et d’importants mouvements de populations, l’ONU estime que la mobilisation internationale doit être à la hauteur de l’urgence afin d’éviter une aggravation de la crise sanitaire. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Ebola en RDC: l’ONU lance un appel urgent pour 1,1 milliard de dollars est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Lutte contre la divagation des animaux à Ouagadougou : La Police municipale intensifie ses actions
items.description: Face à la recrudescence du phénomène de la divagation des animaux dans la cité, la Direction de la Police de la Salubrité et de la Tranquillité Urbaine (DPSTU) de la Police Municipale de Ouagadougou mène quotidiennement des opérations de lutte contre ce fléau dans les différents quartiers de la ville. Durant la saison pluvieuse, période au cours de laquelle le phénomène prend davantage d’ampleur, la DPSTU a intensifié ses interventions afin de lutter efficacement contre la divagation des animaux et de préserver la sécurité, la salubrité et le cadre de vie des populations. Ainsi, au cours des trois derniers mois, notamment juin, juillet et août 2026, ce sont environ deux milles (2000) têtes d’animaux, composées de bovins, de chevaux, d’ovins et de caprins, qui ont été mises en fourrière. Au-delà des risques d’accidents et des nuisances qu’elle occasionne, la divagation des animaux constitue également une préoccupation en matière d’hygiène et de salubrité publique. Elle contribue notamment à la dégradation des espaces verts et à la destruction de la flore urbaine. La Police Municipale de Ouagadougou rappelle à la population l’importance du respect des textes en vigueur, notamment la Loi n°022-2005/AN portant Code de l’hygiène publique au Burkina Faso, ainsi que l’Arrêté n°97-027/MATS/PKAD/CO prescrivant les mesures d’hygiène et de salubrité dans la Ville de Ouagadougou. Elle invite, par conséquent, les propriétaires d’animaux à prendre toutes les dispositions nécessaires afin d’éviter leur divagation dans la ville. La Police Municipale, toujours plus proche de vous ! Service de l’Information et de la Communication.

items.title: Projet agro-écologie de Guédiawaye : l’agriculture urbaine au service des communautés
items.description: Des jeunes de la ville Guédiawaye ont décidé d’aménager un jardin agro-écologique sur un ancien dépotoir autour du lac Tiourour. À travers cette initiative, le projet Agroécologie de Guédiawaye entend œuvrer pour le développement d’une agriculture urbaine. Cette démarche permet aux populations de reverdir leur localité et d’améliorer leur cadre de vie. La surreprésentation des bâtiments et du béton défigure le paysage urbain à Dakar. Cette situation a entraîné un manque d’espaces verts dans les quartiers de Dakar pourtant essentiels à l’amélioration de leur cadre de vie. Ainsi, des jeunes de Guédiawaye ont décidé d’aménager un jardin agro-écologique sur un ancien dépotoir autour du lac Tiourour dans ladite localité. Le dispositif sert à produire des plantules et des pépinières pour accompagner le développement des jardins urbains en ville. L’association « Mon quartier écologique » est aussi impliquée dans la production de graines et de plantules au profit du jardinage urbain. Le projet a démarré en 2021 avec un investissement de 6 millions de FCfa sur fonds propres avec l’appui de la mairie de Wakhinane Nimzatt et de l’Agence de la grande muraille verte. Il consiste à recevoir des déchets organiques pour faire du compost et de l’engrais. En échange, les populations reçoivent une plante, explique Mame Diarra Niang, agronome et promotrice du projet d’agroécologie. « Nous privilégions la culture bio, nous travaillons sur une surface de 500 m². Nous avons une table pour former les pensionnaires en agroécologie et faire des ateliers de pépinière. Nous avons aussi des arbres fruitiers (citronniers et papayers) et, dans le centre, nous avons le box maraîcher (piment, poivron… », a fait savoir la paysagiste. A lire aussi : Tobor, modèle d’une agroécologie tournée vers l’entrepreneuriat Elle a indiqué que l’association mène aussi des formations au profit des jeunes et des femmes de Guédiawaye engagés dans l’agriculture durable. « Nous avons aussi une serre artificielle (tomates, piment pixen et sofia) et des papayers pour les arbres fruitiers, ainsi que des poivrons et des épices pour les Gie de femmes qui s’intéressent à la transformation des produits alimentaires », soutient-elle. Selon la paysagiste, le projet prévoit aussi l’hydroponie, une technique pour faire de la culture hors-sol avec un support en tubes Pvc, où les racines baignent dans une solution nutritive remplie d’intrants. « L’urbanisme galopant va nous forcer à développer le concept de micro-jardinage et de maraîchage pour aider les jeunes et les femmes à développer une activité économique. Le projet Agroécologie offre aussi des kits de jardinage pour perpétuer l’apprentissage de l’agriculture en terrasse », soutient-elle. « Je viens souvent me fournir en plantules de citronnelle, de romarin et de thym pour approvisionner mon micro-jardin sur ma terrasse. J’ai développé un petit commerce en livrant de petits sachets de feuilles de thym et de romarin à des clients pour des tisanes et d’autres mets », a indiqué Abdou Lô, habitant du quartier. Mame Diarra Niang compte bien reproduire ce modèle dans d’autres localités de Dakar avec des jardins communautaires. Toutefois, la paysagiste renseigne que la destruction des filaos sur le littoral de Guédiawaye les prive de sources de matière organique pour développer la production de plantules et d’arbres fruitiers. Selon elle, cette situation peut entraver le projet de développement du micro-jardinage et de l’agriculture urbaine à Dakar. Mamadou Makhfouse NGOM et Fatimata Bintou BA

items.title: Over 400 Pharmacy technicians unemployed as PTAG calls for more jobs, tighter drug controls
items.description: The Pharmacy Technicians Association of Ghana (PTAG) has called on the government to increase the number of pharmacy technicians employed in the public sector to address the growing number of unemployed practitioners. PTAG President Pharmatech Michael Gyamprah said more than 4,000 pharmacy technicians are currently unemployed, with some having completed their training as far back as 2020. He said the Association had worked with the Ministry of Health to secure clearance to employ 150 pharmacy technicians, who are currently undergoing the posting process to their respective districts. Pharmatech Gyamprah made the call at the 17th Annual General Conference of the Pharmacy Technicians Association of Ghana in Sunyani. The conference was held on the theme: “The Role of Pharmacy Technicians in Advancing SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being.” He said although the employment of the 150 technicians was a step in the right direction, the number remained inadequate compared with the thousands of trained technicians awaiting employment. He said the Association was engaging the Ministry of Health to secure additional opportunities for pharmacy technicians. “We therefore call on the government to increase the allocation for all pharmacy practitioners,” he said. Pharmatech Gyamprah also called on the Pharmacy Council to strengthen its supervision of institutions that train pharmacy technicians. He said while Ghana needed more pharmacy professionals, the quality of training must not be compromised. He further urged the Pharmacy Council to strictly enforce laws restricting the dispensing of certain medicines to qualified pharmacy professionals. According to him, non-pharmacy practitioners should not be allowed to dispense Class A and B medicines in pharmacies and hospital dispensaries. He said strict enforcement of the law would help reduce the misuse of antimicrobial medicines. Pharmatech Gyamprah also said the merger between the Ghana Hospital Pharmacists Association (GHOSPA) and PTAG had strengthened cooperation within the pharmacy workforce and improved the provision of pharmaceutical care. He urged pharmacy technicians to accept postings to areas where their services were most needed when employment opportunities became available. The thematic speaker at the conference, Pharmatech Etse Nkukpornu, said corruption in the pharmaceutical sector could be reduced through stronger checks on the procurement and distribution of medicines. He said the procurement of medicines should involve open and competitive tendering among properly registered pharmaceutical companies. “Procurement should not be left in the hands of one person,” he said, stressing the need for trained pharmacy professionals to be involved in the process. “Let’s compare prices against quality. In that case, I’m sure that procurements can be reduced,” he said. Pharmatech Nkukpornu also called for the installation of CCTV cameras in sensitive areas of pharmacies and hospitals, including storerooms, pharmacies and payment points. He said the cameras could help deter the theft of medicines and money. He further called for clear sanctions against workers found taking money from patients at unauthorised locations. Pharmatech Nkukpornu said reducing corruption also required a change in attitude among health workers and members of the public. He said the fight against corruption should not be left to the government alone, adding that everyone had a role to play in ensuring that people could access healthcare without being subjected to unauthorised payments. He said achieving Sustainable Development Goal 3, which seeks to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all, required a collective effort from health workers, the government and the public.

Ce vendredi 28 aout 2026, le forum de la presse du Studio Kalangou revient sur 3 grands sujets de l'actualite : La mise en place du Parlement confederal de l'Alliance des etats du Sahel lors d'une session inaugurale a Niamey, avec 45 deputes. Le Niger se prepare a appliquer la loi sur la tarification des loyers en milieu urbain. Le ministre de l'Urbanisme a rencontre les acteurs du secteur pour preparer la mise en œuvre. Retard ou manque des pluies dans plusieurs localites du Niger, notamment Diffa. La meteo appelle a la prudence avant tout bilan, mais les agriculteurs s'inquietent. Pour analyser ces sujets, nous recevons : Ousseini Issa Djibo , journaliste independant Maimouna Djado , journalistes independants, Arimi Abba Kiari , journaliste a la radio Alternative. Tarnane Foudai Ahmed, a la moderation.

items.title: Welcome to the Scrolling Backlash
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube A lot of people are getting tired of their phone—they’re sick of the algorithms and overwhelmed by what can feel like a loss of control. The Atlantic staff writer Julie Beck dug into why and how people are trying to renegotiate their relationships with technology. She and our colleagues just released a five-part podcast series called How to Touch Grass , and in this episode, Galaxy Brain host Charlie Warzel talks with Beck about why people are nostalgic for the pre-internet days, how our brains are changing, and the good that can come from getting lost. The following is a transcript of the episode: Charlie Warzel: How does the phone make you feel? How does a TikTok binge make you feel, or even just, like, a before-bed scrolling session that we all have? Julie Beck: Oh, sick. Absolutely sick. It’s like when the aliens get you, right? They take you up and then they probe you, or they do whatever they do, and then when you come back down, you don’t know what happened. It’s erased. It’s lost time. So I feel like I have emerged from lost time and like what happened during that time is unclear, but I don’t feel good. Warzel: I don’t know that I have the amnesia part of it, but it promotes self-loathing in a way that like truly no other activity does because it just feels like a deletion of my one precious life. I’m Charlie Warzel, and this is Galaxy Brain , a show where today we’re gonna answer a question. Maybe it’s even the question of the online age. How can we live lives where we use tech and don’t let it use us? This is the animating question of How to Touch Grass , a new podcast series by my colleagues here at The Atlantic . Over five episodes, Julie Beck and her co-host and producer, Natalie Brennan, explore what exactly is happening in this moment that has so many of us out there feeling like we need to renegotiate our relationships to our technology. At the beginning of this year, I made a few predictions about trends that we might see, and one of them was that there would be what I was calling a scrolling backlash. That people are just really tired of their phones, of the algorithmic internet, of this idea that they’re being manipulated all the time, and that their attention is being directed towards things that don’t make them feel good or whole or happy. Now, as predictions go, this is a pretty safe one, but it’s really been borne out in recent months. These things are hard to measure, but you can just feel it out there in the world. In the artists who are asking that people leave their phones at home or in their pockets at concerts, in the genuine concern over whether younger generations are going to be able to read like older generations. And while the data-center backlash that we’re seeing right now is complicated, and it’s about a lot of things, including AI, I also see that as an outgrowth of this larger frustration about the role that big tech is playing in our lives and the way that people just feel this fuzzy loss of agency right now. It’s a loss that just can’t be separated from the devices that we use. How to Touch Grass digs into so many of the ideas that I’ve been trying to poke at here in the first year of this podcast. Our motto here at Galaxy Brain is that we pay attention to where we pay attention, which also happens to be exactly what I found so valuable about Julie and Natalie’s work. And so I decided to bring Julie on here today to talk about this moment and to talk about what she’s learned in this series. How badly have our attention spans actually been fractured? How has she reevaluated her relationship to all of her devices? Is the backlash that we’re feeling and seeing right now justified? And crucially, where might we go from here? Julie joins me now to talk about it all. [ Music ] Warzel: Julie, welcome to Galaxy Brain . Julie Beck: Hi, Charlie. Thanks for having me. Warzel: So let’s talk about this. Let’s talk about the touch-grass moment that I think we are in. Even even the phrase itself, right? Why is “touching grass” something that people are talking about? And what made you want to just dig in and report on it? Beck: Yes. So we had originally thought about calling the season How to Log Off , but that’s not as fun. But I think it also speaks to just a sort of general renegotiation that people are doing right now between how much they actually want to be on their devices and how much they actually want to be inhabiting the embodied world around you and the grass and the trees and the people and everybody around you. We wanted to look at like the various shifts that are happening both in the culture of the internet itself and the technology itself but also the shifts in the culture of how people are thinking about their devices and how they’re talking about them, and how much they want to use them. Warzel: Why did you feel like this was a project you wanted to embark on? Beck: I have deleted and re-downloaded TikTok on my phone roughly four to five times. Warzel: Nice. Beck: And it’s usually like my friend ends up sending me a Lord of the Rings meme and then you click it, and to click it, to see it, you have to re-download the app, and they get me every time. Warzel: It’s a gateway drug. Beck: Lord of the Rings memes are the gateway drug kids. But no, I noticed something happening maybe six-ish months ago when whenever I was on my last round of being on TikTok, which is: Every time I would go on there, I would get nothing but reels of “how to be offline more”, like “how to live more analog,” “how to heal your attention span” on this app where I was actively in the process of degrading my attention span. So I thought that irony was interesting, and so I think there was a shift that I was just sensing within myself, but also in conversations that I would have with people in real life and in what I was seeing online of people really trying to just be on their phones less, be on social media less. And I was curious why now, when obviously we’ve had smartphones for a very long time, we’ve had the internet for a very long time, we’ve had social media for a long time. Warzel: What is the answer to that? Why now? Beck: Why now? I think some of it is that we’ve had it for long enough that the shine’s off the apple, right? And I think some of it is a confluence of these different bigger conversations. Obviously, there’s like a big push by many to get kids off of social media, right? Or there’s lawsuits against Instagram, and What is Instagram doing to our mental health? And so I do think that those things have leaked down in some way, but also even TikTok, right, has been pretty popular for a few years. We’ve had a few years of living in this sort of algorithmically optimized short-form-video environment. And it’s gotten to the point where maybe people have had enough experience with it that they’re starting to see the effects in their own lives and like starting to question that rather than just, Oh, isn’t this fun? I can watch Lord of the Rings memes . And I think combining that with the sort of arrival of AI on the scene, right? And seeing all of these extreme stories about people replacing relationships with AI, using AI as a friend or a lover—God forbid—I think there’s been a sort of opposite, if not equal, reaction to valuing more the embodied world and the real social relationships that we had. So I think people are reacting in part to the sort of evolution of the internet culture and social-media environment and the arrival of this new technology that’s really like getting its little tendrils into every area of our lives. Warzel: So one of the episodes—to pivot here—explores nostalgia, which I think is a very big part of all of this hand-wringing that we are all personally going through, right? Is this moment different from others? Are we doing something uniquely awful to our brains that none of our ancestors ever did? And when you talk about nostalgia, there’s particularly a focus on young people who weren’t really around to have that pre-internet life. In that episode though, you have this moment where you describe a time that you got truly and deeply lost. And so it struck me that your co-host, who’s slightly younger than you, never had that experience. She’d never been an adult without a smartphone. And so what do you think is the value of being in a place where you don’t have a phone to save you? Are we losing something when we don’t experience that vulnerability? Beck: Yes and no. I do look back on it with a fondness. I would no longer—unless my phone died, I guess—I would no longer ever be in a position where I simply had to throw myself on the mercy of strangers and hope that they helped me. If I were lost somewhere, I can just follow the blue dot until I figured it out. And I don’t know that I yearn to go back to that. In some ways, that wasn’t very safe. I was like a young woman traveling alone in a country where I didn’t speak the language, and I had no idea where I was and no way to really communicate with anyone. I’m not mad that I have Google Maps and I have some sort of safety features to keep me safe when I go places. And I do think we have lost a little bit of something of just, kind of, being where you are and letting the experience be what it is. And those opportunities for connection, right? I would not ask someone for help. I would just use my phone. So I feel ambivalent about it. And I would say that, in fact, ambivalence is the primary emotion of the season and of just today’s technology. Warzel: So there’s this stat that you reference—because we’re talking a little bit about people who haven’t had access to a life without smartphones—and I found it honestly just bracing, maybe even troubling, but the stat is essentially that 60 percent of Gen Z wishes that they could return to a time before everyone was “plugged in.” And nostalgia’s a very common thing. You get into this in the episode. Everyone has nostalgia for some period of time. But Gen Z’s nostalgia for this time before they were alive, it seems like something else to me. Like it seems like a genuine indictment of this moment that we are in. How do you read that stat? What does that make you feel when you hear that? Beck: I take that status as not actually indicative of if you presented them with a time machine and were like, “You can go live in 1985,” that they would go in there and live in 1985. I don’t think they actually want to give up on all of the other things that have happened since then. But it’s just this sense of like, Something in my life isn’t working. I attribute it to this device , and it’s being expressed as like, I just wish we could go back . But I don’t think it actually means they wish they could go back. Warzel: Yeah. I think one thing that I’m trying to figure out is: Do you feel like it’s just an escapist phenomenon in that way, or just a coping mechanism? Or do you think it actually leads to or has the potential to lead to a genuine backlash or push or protest against some of this stuff. I think about just the physical-media boom, like a push to do some things in a more analog way, even if it is kind of “niche” or “hipster,” or whatever you wanna call it. Beck: Yeah, I feel like maybe I went into this thinking it is just kind of an escapist fantasy, in the way that somebody might be like, I should’ve been born in the 1920s. I would have made such a great flapper , or whatever it may be. But the expert who we interviewed for that episode, Clay Routledge, he studies nostalgia, and his whole take on nostalgia overall is that it’s about the future as much as it is about the past. So it’s not just warm feelings for the past and like, What a nice time I had doing whatever, but it’s also telling you something important about the way that you want to live now and going forward. And so, especially seeing what you’re talking about: the sort of rise in people buying physical media again, people giving up their smartphones for dumb phones. I do think it is inspiring some level of actual behavioral change. And even if you don’t go so far as to get a dumb phone and try to LARP your life like it’s the ’90s, I think it still tells you something important about what you value and maybe smaller shifts that you do want to make in how you relate to technology and how you set up your life. Warzel: If there’s one real theme of How to Touch Grass , I think it’s that the tools that we use change us, obviously, in these unexpected ways, right? Our habits, how we see ourselves, how we see other people, how we talk to each other—everything. And the show explores this from anxiety to body image. And I wanna play you another clip from your own show here. Sophie Gilbert: I don’t think anyone is supposed to see their own face as much as we do now. I think about this a lot, like how our ancestors would have felt like catching a glance at themselves in a lake. And instead we’re front-facing camera, front-facing camera, front-facing camera , and it’s weird. It’s warping our brains. Warzel: That was our fellow staff writer, Sophie Gilbert, talking to you. What strikes me a bit about being hyper-connected is that, in theory, the access to abundant information that we have should be a good thing, I think. And it just doesn’t seem to work that way in practice. Like the way that we can learn anything, but we tend to gravitate towards information that confirms our biases, right? And pushes us deeper down whatever rabbit hole. Or how we can learn anything about our bodies and then it pushes us to go and Google these things that lead to more and more anxiety. The thing that Sophie gets at in that clip, really, is something that you hear a lot of people say, which is, We were never supposed to have this much access to ourselves, other people, information , and yet we hold that up as: That’s the beauty of the internet. That’s the great thing—more, more, more, abundance, the Library of Alexandria at your fingertips, whatever, right? But what do you feel like this access is doing to people? Beck: I think what I’ve been thinking a lot about since wrapping up the interviews for that season is that there are costs to every way of living. And what is happening is that the design of our technology—the design of these apps of smartphones, or honestly the design of society in general right now—is pushing you to accept a certain set of costs and trade-offs. And that is: constant distraction and the slow degradation of your attention span and maybe some body-image problems in exchange for the most abundance of entertainment, connection, communication, relationships, information that you could possibly imagine. And that is a trade-off that you may decide is worth making, right? At this moment in time, maybe I’m waiting for the bus and it is worth it to me to degrade my attention span a little and be entertained. But are you actually consciously choosing those costs, or are you just sort of being pushed by default into making those trade-offs? And there are trade-offs to inserting more distance between yourself and your phone as well. The phone is kind of where the people are, and so if you want to be on your phone less, then maybe you are gonna be a little bit less connected to long-distance loved ones, or maybe you’re gonna have a harder time figuring out what is the weather today, or getting that information that you need right now about how to get into the concert venue. It’s like there are costs either way. However, all of society is kind of set up to push you towards one set of costs. And I think people are starting to question that a little bit. Warzel: Yeah, and I think if there’s an insidious part of the Big Tech experience, right, it is making people feel when they’re using these things like there aren’t any trade-offs. They are marketed as Connection is a universal good or This thing is a universal productivity increaser , and you should feel this way about them. Some of what we’re feeling in this moment, I think, is maybe not fully being gaslit, but you’re experiencing the trade-offs, the costs, and you’re sort of conditioned not to think that there are any. So you’re like, What’s wrong with me that I can’t get a handle on this, that I can’t get a handle on my attention span or feel this way? And I think it’s a bit of, like: No, no, no, no, no. You have to do that inventory of the give-and-take. And you also have to know that it’s not a fair fight and that’s okay. You just need to be armed with that information. I think that we’re not as much these days. Beck: Yeah. Well, I also think a lot about the way that—a lot of the response to this, a lot of the current movement to log off or do whatever is very draconian. It’s like, I’m getting rid of my phone and I’m getting a dumbphone, and I’m never gonna look at social media ever again . Because I think the reasonable alternative, unfortunately, is that you just kind of have to manage it forever. Like you said, the deck is stacked against you. These companies are not going to decide that they want less of your attention, wake up one morning and decide that they’ve had enough. And so it feels for a lot of people that the fantasy is to just completely leave it behind forever and walk into the sea and live an analog existence. And if you don’t want to live that way, or if it is not reasonable to live that way, which I think for most people it’s not, then unfortunately the answer is just kind of dealing with that push-and-pull and designing something—it’s very DIY, right?—it’s designing something for yourself with your phone, with your technology that works for you. And it requires kind of constant upkeep, constant management, and constant resistance of the forces that are trying to suck you in, and that’s kind of exhausting. Warzel: Yeah, absolutely. You devoted an episode to the ways that technology is changing the way that we learn. And I think that people can feel that disruption right now, especially with chatbots. I wanna play a clip from an interview you did with Michelle Miller, who’s a cognitive psychologist at Northern Arizona University. Michelle Miller: I think that teaching another human being how to do something, that is one of the highest and best expressions of humanity that there is. It’s one of the best and most positive ways that we interact with and contribute to one another. So I do think it comes back to that core, our self-agency and our connection to this great web of humanity. I mean, it comes about through learning. Warzel: I love the great web of humanity. Beck: Me too. Warzel: I hope we can preserve it. So what I take away from this is: Learning is social. And what’s interesting about that is the current internet is full of other people, other people’s opinions, broadcasting yourself for other people. It’s social. But it’s also a lot of synthetic stuff, a lot of synthetic people, a lot of people behaving in ways that they wouldn’t, or in antisocial ways. And it’s also this medium that very clearly isolates us. And so as you’re exploring this, do you feel like we’re losing something fundamental here when it comes to learning? Or is it just a different way of learning that will produce different results? Where have you come out on all that? Beck: I think that doing this series also reminded me, and especially when it comes to learning, all of the genuinely good things that I do get from technology. I like to knit and crochet. And where do I go to learn how to do a new crochet stitch? I go on YouTube because they have a video and it’s perfect and I can see it and I can do it. So I get a lot out of that, right? Or for my job, I read a lot of PDFs on the internet to obtain knowledge. Warzel: Hell yeah. Beck: And that is very useful. And I think that, like Michelle was saying, learning is extremely human. And at one point, she mentioned that learning is the way that you build the brain that you live in. It’s not just going to school and doing your multiplication tables and then growing up to calculate all of your tips on a calculator for the rest of your life. You cannot help but experience the world through the black box of your own mind. And so to build your own mind is building how you perceive the world, how you interact with the world. And so to outsource that to a machine to me is just anathema. Warzel: And, too, I found this really interesting talking to educators, as I’m covering AI, but the idea that no one likes writing the whatever, the five-paragraph essay that you learn how to do. Beck: Yeah, yeah, yeah. “In this essay, I will …” Warzel: But at the same time, it’s actually helping your brain understand like, When I encounter new information, these are the programs that I can run to figure out what I think about it . It is just scaffolding, in order to help yourself work through a complex idea and sort it. And I love that idea of, it is elated to your brain’s perception; you live in the world built around your own critical thinking. To sort of expand on that, in the series you talk a lot about attention. You end up doing an experiment near the end of the series based off of finding a baseline of where your attention is at right now. And I don’t wanna spoil it, but I’m wondering what made you wanna do this experience? What was worrying you about your own attention? Beck: It’s a lot of what I’ve heard from many people, which is just like feeling my attention pulled in so many different directions, or just having a baseline feeling of buzzy stimulation and not like the calm focus on one thing that I know at some point I was capable of and wanting to see if the phone was indeed the culprit and if I could find that again. So yeah, I did an experiment which was based on an actual study that came out like a year ago, where they blocked the internet on people’s phones for two weeks and tested their attention before and after. I got in touch with one of the researchers who did that study, and he kind of helped me do my own version of it where I took the same measures that they did. And I blocked almost everything, for 23 hours a day and did that for two weeks and then took the test again so Warzel: Again, I don’t wanna totally spoil things for people, but I think what we can say here is that in a short amount of time, there were—correct me if I’m wrong—somewhat dramatic results, or at least meaningful results. Beck: Yeah. Warzel: I want to end here asking how your relationship to your devices has changed while exploring all of this stuff. Do you feel a little more positive about all of it, just having had the experience of immersing yourself in this and with these experts who like to figure it out? A big part of the challenge for a lot of people, I think, is not really knowing what to feel good or bad about. I got a sense going through the series that you’re orienting yourself to this problem, and sometimes that’s like all we need, when it is so pervasive. But how has your relationship to the devices changed? Beck: I think you’re right. I think I have a little bit more clarity around my values and my ideal scenario. I’m not always living up to it, obviously. But I think for instance, for me, I don’t really use AI. Maybe that will change, but if it does change, I’m gonna be real careful about how I want to use it and in what very specific scenarios. And one of the things that Jenny Odell said and we interviewed her for the attention episode was to think about things as an experiment. [ Phone ringing ] Kostadin Kushlev: Hello. Brennan: Hi, I’m Natalie. I’m Julie’s producer. I’m also gonna be sitting in on this call. Kushlev: Hi, Natalie. Beck: Hey, Kosta. It’s Julie. How are you? Kushlev: Pretty good. How are you doing? Beck: I’m doing okay! So, can we just dive right in? Kushlev: Yes. Beck: And tell me, before I started the experiment, how was my baseline attention span? Kushlev: So your score was about three, 3.02. Beck: Is that good? Good for a 35-year-old? Good, bad? Kushlev: That’s pretty good. Essentially, you did about how our participants did. It’s a little closer to the level you might see in young adulthood or for somebody in their 60s. ( Laughs. ) Beck: ( Laughs. ) Okay. Humbling. Humbling. Kushlev: Yes. Yes. But, you know, but once we get to your post score— Beck: Yes, let’s do it. Kushlev: — things really change. Beck: The big reveal. Kushlev: Yes. Beck: What changed? Kushlev: So your post score was actually hugely better. So it was 3.8. And that is much bigger improvement than we saw on average in our study. So your improvement is about four to five times bigger than what the average participant in our study gained. Brennan: Go Julie! Beck: Write it down, Natalie. Write it down. ( Laughs. ) Brennan: I’m taking notes. Kushlev: Yeah. So you did really well on that. Beck: Amazing, I think. Is 3.1 to 3.8 good? Have I reversed my cognitive decline? Or how would you characterize that? Kushlev: You’re basically off the charts. Beck: ( Laughs. ) Kushlev : But it might take a while to reap the benefits of this improved attention. Beck: Right. And it’ll probably go away if I just start scrolling Instagram again. Kushlev: Right. Yeah. Brennan: ( Laughs. ) Kushlev: It’s certainly not a permanent increase. But I do like to point out that, you know, just taking a two-week break and not even a complete break from your phone, just sort of like reducing your use, can actually improve that ability to sustain attention. Our lives are just like so tied to these devices, so sometimes the question might be: Have we like essentially permanently damaged our, you know— Beck: Yeah. Kushlev: —brains? Like, have we changed our neurobiology and so forth? And so this seems to suggest that no, there is a way out. So it might be worth doing some of those digital-detox interventions. [ Music ] Beck: Thank you so much, Kosta. It was great chatting with you! Kushlev: Alright, thank you, bye. Brennan: Bye! Brennan: Julie? Beck: Mm-hmm. Brennan: How do you feel about that? Beck: Unbearably smug. No, no, no. I’m just kidding. No, I feel relieved, honestly. Like, even if the true effect size isn’t as big as it seemed, ’cause I am just one person; it’s not, you know, a full scientific study— Brennan: Yeah. Beck: —it still feels really good to know that it’s possible to improve so quickly. Brennan: Right. Beck: So it’s actually kind of wild that you can do something as simple as this and, like, bounce back so quickly. Brennan: Are you going to keep using the Brick? Like, how are you feeling about—where’s your relationship at between you and your phone right now? Beck: My relationship with my phone is cordial. We’re not—it’s not warm— Brennan: ( Laughs. ) Beck : —but it’s not cold. We’re cordial. We’re friendly acquaintances. Brennan: That sounds like how people describe their exes. Beck: Yeah. And, well, we haven’t broken up. It really is—it’s a situationship— Brennan: Totally. Beck: —that is ongoing forever. No, I’m definitely gonna continue using the Brick, and I have been still. Twenty-three hours a day? You know, maybe not. Brennan: Yeah. Beck: I have been Bricking my phone, at a minimum, before bed, so I can’t doom scroll right before I sleep, and I can’t look at my emails or Instagram the second that I regain consciousness. So that does help. [ Music ] But I would say that throughout this, I kept thinking about my favorite poet, Mary Oliver, and one thing that she wrote was, “To pay attention, this is our endless and proper work.” Brennan: That’s beautiful. Beck: So this season, I think what I’ve learned is: Your attention is your life. And I think on some level I knew that already, but after this experiment, I’ve really been feeling it. Brennan: We started this season because we wanted to understand why so many people were feeling the pull to log off, right? We’ve explored a lot of the ways in which the internet can pull you into thoughtless patterns, whether it’s the way Instagram makes us feel bad about our bodies or the way that AI chatbots can send us into an anxious spiral. But it seems like what we are maybe actually looking for, right now, is ways to be more thoughtful. Beck: Yeah, I wanted to feel more thoughtful about my life. I wanted to not to feel as much like I’m literally giving my life away to things that I don’t even care about. I wanted to stop nickel-and-diming the moments of my life away. Brennan: Being intentional about where you give your attention. [ Music ] Beck: This episode was hosted by me, Julie Beck, and co-hosted and produced by Natalie Brennan, with production help from Elena Schwartz. Our editors are Claudine Ebeid and Jocelyn Frank. Fact-check by Gisela Salim-Peyer. Our engineers are Rob Smierciak and Miguel Carrascal. Rob also composed some of the music for this show. The executive producer of audio is Claudine Ebeid, and the managing editor of audio is Andrea Valdez. Warzel: Thank you again to my guest, Julie Beck. items.title: SECP introduces unified framework for 'faster and easier' entry into Pakistan's capital market
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has introduced a unified digital investor onboarding framework to make entry into Pakistan’s capital market “faster and easier by reducing repetitive verification, simplifying documentation and setting clear timelines for opening investor accounts”. The framework aims particularly to facilitate first-time and digital investors, with ‘Sehl/Sahulat’ accounts to be processed within one working day and normal accounts within two working days, according to an SECP statement issued on Friday. “Applicants will receive tracking IDs, while any deficiencies will be communicated within the prescribed timeframe and reasons for rejection provided in writing,” it stated. The statement said the initiative was part of the SECP’s broader drive to expand retail participation, particularly among young Pakistanis, and increase the country’s capital-market investor base to 2.5 million. “Our focus is to remove entry barriers and use technology to make the investor journey simpler, faster and more accessible,” SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu was quoted as saying. “The objective is to unlock the significant untapped potential of Pakistan’s capital market by broadening participation, particularly among the youth, and building a deeper and more inclusive market,“ he elaborated. The framework standardises onboarding requirements across “securities brokers, asset management companies, insurers and other regulated intermediaries, creating a more consistent investor experience across the regulated financial sector,” the statement said. According to the SECP, the key feature of the framework is the elimination of repetitive customer verification. Where prescribed verification has already been completed by an eligible regulated financial institution or notified third party, intermediaries can rely on that verification instead of requiring investors to repeat the process. “The framework also enables API-based straight-through processing and digital onboarding, including instant UIN issuance and opening of CDC sub-accounts, reducing paperwork and manual intervention,” the SECP said. A few months ago, the government of Pakistan also established the Capital Market Development Fund (CMDF), aimed at promoting financial literacy, expanding financial inclusion and increasing retail investor participation in the capital markets across the country.

items.title: Dutch court hands life sentence to Rwandan man for genocide role
items.description: A Dutch court has sentenced a Rwandan man to life in prison for his role in the murder of thousands during the 1994 genocide in the Central African country. The Hague district court found Eugene N guilty of war crimes and genocide on Friday, and issued the sentence. Judges called his conduct a “significant lack of respect for human dignitiy and for human life,” and said that only a life sentence would serve justice “to the immense suffering that has been inflicted on the victims and the bereaved families”. Named only as Eugene N, the suspect helped ransack and burn homes in two mostly Tutsi communities, before taking part in a mob that descended on roughly 3,000 Tutsis sheltering in a stadium in Mbazi in April of 1994. He directed the Hutu attackers to let no one escape and threw a grenade into the crowd, the court said. Survivors of the initial attack were later beaten and hacked to death. Eugene N, variously reported to be 66 or 67 years old, fled the Netherlands in 1998 and later became a Dutch citizen. Rwanda sought his extradition in 2014, but the Netherlands’ law shields nationals from being handed over. Prosecutors opened their case in 2020, questioning more than 30 witnesses before arresting him in 2024. Eugene N denied his involvement, his defence portraying him as having tried to stop the violence and lost dozens of relatives himself. His representatives called him “a broken man”. Prosectutors countered, “If the horrific crimes of the suspect … do not deserve a life sentence, then what does?” Rwanda’s 1994 genocide killed more 800,000 people, mostly Tutsis, in roughly three months of violence directed by Hutu ethnonationalist leaders. A United Nations tribunal prosecuted leading organisers, but European courts have since pursued lower-level suspects under universal jurisdiction, which allows atrocities and war crimes to be prosecuted regardless of where they occurred. Dutch courts have convicted other genocide suspects, and in some cases, extradited them to Rwanda.

items.title: Garde à vue de Sébastien Delogu : l'affaire qui perturbe l'été idyllique des Insoumis
items.description: Le depute des Bouches-du-Rhone Sebastien Delogu a passe plusieurs heures en garde a vue le 27 août au commissariat central de Marseille. Sorti peu avant 23 heures par une porte derobee, accompagne de son avocat, il a rapidement remercie sur X ses soutiens ainsi que « les forces de l'ordre qui se sont comportees de maniere irreprochable ». Il a precise etre rentre chez lui pour se reposer et s'exprimer bientot. Versions contradictoires et plaintes croisees L'incident remonte au lundi 24 août. Trois policiers du Service interdepartemental de securisation des transports en commun cherchaient un suspect de vol de montre dans l'immeuble ou reside l'elu. Selon les agents, Delogu se serait oppose physiquement a leur entree, les traitant notamment de « bande de fatigues » ou de « trou du c*** », et aurait affirme « La Republique, c'est moi », celebre phrase assenee par Jean-Luc Melenchon lors d'une perquisition en octobre 2018. 🇫🇷 FLASH | Les images de l'altercation entre le député LFI Sébastien Delogu et des policiers à Marseille. pic.twitter.com/weBRqYREs6 https://t.co/RhC7upVxbJ — Cerfia (@CerfiaFR) August 26, 2026 Ils ont depose plainte pour outrage a personne depositaire de l'autorite publique. De son cote, le depute affirme que les policiers, en civil, n'avaient pas decline leur identite. Il decrit des insultes (« tu pues de la g*** », phrase qu'il avait lui-meme dite a une militante feministe quelques mois plus tot) et un coup sur la poitrine. Il a porte plainte contre X pour violences volontaires et saisi l'IGPN. La video qui circule est partielle et ne tranche pas le litige. Les reactions politique n'ont pas tarde et l'elu, qui n'etait pas present a la photo des cadres LFI lors de l'universite d'ete du mouvement a ete soutenu par des elus de son parti tandis que ses adversaires ont denonce son attitude vis-a-vis des policiers a l'image de l'eurodepute RN Matthieu Valet qui a dit son « soutien total aux 3 policiers » tandis que la ministre deleguee chargee de l'egalite entre les femmes et les hommes et de la Lutte contre les discriminations a declare le 28 août : « La France insoumise a mis la violence au cœur d'une strategie politique ». «La France insoumise a mis la violence au cœur d'une stratégie politique», alerte Aurore Bergé, ministre déléguée chargée de l'Égalité entre les femmes et les hommes et de la Lutte contre les discriminations, après la garde à vue de Sébastien Delogu, dans #LaGrandeInterview pic.twitter.com/CaW3lc3KZp — CNEWS (@CNEWS) August 28, 2026 L'elu, deja condamne en 2025 pour violences et convoque le 21 octobre dans une autre affaire, comparaîtra le 13 novembre devant le tribunal correctionnel de Marseille. Cet episode vient troubler un ete que les Insoumis esperaient plus serein, alors que la rentree politique approche et que son universite d'ete a ete un succes.

items.title: Urgent/ BCRG Vs Syndicat : le tribunal relaxe les trois syndicalistes et déboute le parquet et la partie civile
items.description: Le tribunal correctionnel de Kaloum a rendu ce vendredi 28 août 2026 sa décision dans l’affaire opposant trois membres de la délégation syndicale de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG) à Daouda Sankhon, aide de camp du gouverneur de l’institution. Poursuivis notamment pour des faits présumés d’« outrage à agent, violences et voies de fait », les trois syndicalistes ont finalement été renvoyés des fins de la poursuite et relaxés par le tribunal. Les charges jugées non constituées Dans sa décision, le tribunal a estimé que les éléments constitutifs du délit d’outrage, prévu par l’article 658 du Code pénal, n’étaient pas réunis à la charge des prévenus. Il a également considéré que les éléments constitutifs des faits de violences ou voies de fait, prévus par l’article 240 du Code pénal, n’étaient pas établis. Le tribunal a ainsi conclu qu’ « aucun acte matériel constitutif d'outrage ou de violence ou encore de voies de fait n'est établi ni personnellement imputable » aux prévenus. En conséquence, les trois syndicalistes ont été renvoyés des fins de la poursuite et relaxés. Le ministère public débouté de ses réquisitions Cette décision vient également contredire les réquisitions formulées la veille par le ministère public. Lors de l’audience du jeudi 27 août, le procureur Issouf Fofana avait requis que les trois prévenus soient déclarés coupables d’outrage à agent et condamnés chacun au paiement d’un million de francs guinéens d’amende. Le tribunal a finalement débouté le ministère public de ses réquisitions. La demande de 100 millions rejetée Sur l’action civile, le tribunal a reçu Daouda Sankhon en sa constitution de partie civile, tout en la déclarant mal fondée. Sa demande de condamnation des trois syndicalistes au paiement de 100 millions de francs guinéens à titre de dommages et intérêts a ainsi été rejetée. Le tribunal a également rejeté la demande de comparution formulée au cours de la procédure et mis les dépens à la charge de la partie civile. Retour sur les faits L’affaire remonte au 6 août 2026, lorsque plusieurs travailleurs de la BCRG, dont les trois prévenus, s’étaient rendus auprès du gouverneur Karamo Kaba pour faire entendre des revendications syndicales. Vêtus de rouge, les syndicalistes souhaitaient notamment obtenir une rencontre avec le gouverneur autour de leurs revendications portant sur leurs conditions de vie et de travail ainsi que sur la signature du protocole d’accord 2026. L’accès au bureau du gouverneur leur avait alors été refusé par son aide de camp, Daouda Sankhon, à l’origine de la plainte. À la barre, les trois prévenus avaient rejeté les accusations portées contre eux. Le plaignant avait, de son côté, affirmé que Momo Camara avait poussé la porte à deux reprises, tout en précisant que les syndicalistes ne l’avaient ni insulté ni touché. Après les réquisitions du parquet et les plaidoiries de la défense, le tribunal avait mis l’affaire en délibéré. Ce vendredi, il a finalement tranché en faveur des prévenus, en prononçant leur relaxe et en rejetant aussi bien les réquisitions du ministère public que la demande indemnitaire de la partie civile.

items.title: 10 of 12 parties prequalified for Fesco privatisation, K-Electric withdraws
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Privatisation Commission Board on Friday approved the prequalification of 10 out of 12 interested parties (IPs) for the sale of Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco), after K-Electric (KE) withdrew its papers and a lone Chinese firm failed to demonstrate sufficient interest in the competition. The development came after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed the relevant authorities to adopt a “comprehensive strategy” earlier this month to attract international investors for the privatisation of state-owned power distribution companies (Discos) and complete the restructuring of the Privatisation Commission within one month. Informed sources said KE, the country’s only privatised power utility, had decided to withdraw rather than risk being disqualified due to the non-availability of its financial accounts for the past two years — a key requirement. They said the company would bid for another distribution company (Disco) as part of a consortium with Shahryar Chishti’s AsiaPak Investments, one of KE’s major shareholders. “K-Electric has withdrawn its Expression of Interest (EOI) for Fesco’s privatisation,” a KE spokesperson confirmed when contacted. He added that the decision was taken because the Disco’s audited financial statements were not yet available, pending finalisation of the company’s Multi-Year Tariff (MYT), which was beyond KE’s control. “We remain committed to pursuing opportunities that maximise value for our stakeholders“, he said. On the other hand, Jiang Xi Electric Power Construction of China did not meet the prequalification criteria, as it filed its EOI in Chinese rather than English on the last day of the deadline, despite repeated requests to submit it in English. The board meeting, presided over by Prime Minister’s Adviser on Privatisation and Privatisation Commission Chairman Muhammad Ali, approved all other prospective bidders for the next stage. The board was informed that a total of 12 EOIs had been received for Fesco. After evaluating the submissions against the approved prequalification criteria, the financial adviser recommended 10 IPs for prequalification. Three are from Turkiye — Aktor Elektrik Enerji Yatırımları San ve Tic AŞ, Genvera Enerji AŞ (Celik Group) and Cengiz Enerji Sanayii ve Ticaret AŞ. The remaining seven Pakistani groups are Engro Energy Limited; Sapphire Fibres Limited, Hub Power Holdings, Lucky Cement and Metro Ventures; Shirazi Investments (Pvt) Limited (Atlas Group); Maple Leaf Cement and Kohinoor Textile; the Pakgen Limited Consortium, comprising Nishat Mills, Nishat Power, Nishat Chunian, Lalpir, Pak Elektron Ltd and Kohinoor Energy; and Artistic Milliners (Private) Limited. The prequalified parties will now proceed to the next stage of the transaction in accordance with the approved process, including access to the Virtual Data Room (VDR) for detailed buy-side due diligence. The board also approved the reconstitution of its Audit and Risk, Human Resources, Investment and Legal committees. The commission said the privatisation aims to improve operational efficiency, modernise distribution infrastructure, strengthen customer service, reduce losses and support a more financially sustainable power sector. Over time, these measures will help create the conditions for more competitive electricity distribution and affordable, reliable power for consumers, it added. Fesco is among the three electricity distribution companies in Disco Batch-I privatisation, alongside Gujranwala Electric Power Company ( Gepco ), which attracted 11 EOIs, most of them also in the run for Fesco and Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco). The deadline for submission of EOIs for Iesco is September 7, 2026. The Privatisation Commission said it would ensure an open, transparent and competitive privatisation process, undertaken in the public interest and in support of the federal government’s wider power-sector reform agenda. Earlier this week, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority notified sweeping guaranteed performance and overall performance standards for all Discos after more than two decades, to ensure compliance even after going into private hands under the ongoing privatisation process. The new Performance Standards (Distribution) Regulations 2026, issued by the regulator after almost two years of consultations with stakeholders, replace the Discos Performance Rules 2005. Under the new standards, utilities will, for the first time, face mandatory consumer compensation, besides heavy fines, if they fail to meet strict deadlines for restoring power after blackouts, replacing faulty meters, addressing voltage fluctuations, providing new connections and other services.

items.title: How couple ended up getting married on Las Vegas flight
items.description: A couple travelling to Las Vegas for a private elopement unexpectedly found themselves getting married mid-flight after Southwest Airlines crew members turned their journey into a surprise wedding ceremony. Sara Arroyo Montalvo and her partner had planned to exchange vows privately after arriving in Las Vegas. However, after flight attendants learnt about their plans, they decided to organise an impromptu ceremony aboard the aircraft. The wedding took place on August 13 in front of 178 passengers, with the plane’s captain officiating the ceremony. The captain was also an ordained minister. The crew went a step further by creating wedding accessories from items available on the aircraft. Montalvo was given a veil and a one-ply wedding dress made from toilet paper, while coffee stir sticks were used to create her bouquet. Reflecting on the unexpected turn of events, Montalvo wrote, “Fate couldn’t have been more aligned,” noting that it was the couple’s first time flying with Southwest Airlines. She also expressed her gratitude to the crew for transforming what was supposed to be an intimate elopement into an unforgettable celebration. “Thank you from the bottom of our hearts for an unforgettable flight!” she wrote. Photos from the ceremony showed the couple exchanging vows in the aircraft aisle as fellow passengers watched and celebrated with them. The unusual wedding quickly attracted attention online, with social media users praising the airline crew for helping create a memorable experience for the newlyweds. The spontaneous ceremony also prompted questions from some users about the legal details of getting married in the air, including where the marriage licence would be issued and how the necessary paperwork would be completed. The couple’s unusual wedding comes amid other reports of people choosing unconventional venues for their big day, including another couple who recently got married at the McDonald’s restaurant where they worked. items.title: JAMB lists 3 reasons candidates miss out on matriculation list
items.description: The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB has explained three reasons candidates may not find their names on its matriculation list. JAMB gave the explanation in an explainer video shared on its official X handle on Friday, highlighting the issues candidates should check if their names are missing. According to the board, the first reason is the most common, while the third is the most important. “Number one is the most common, while number three is the most important. You have not accepted your admission on JAMB CAPS or your admission status reads not admitted,” JAMB said. The board said candidates whose admission status shows “not admitted” should return to their institutions to have their admissions processed. “If it reads not admitted, return to your institution to process your admission,” it stated. JAMB also explained that a candidate’s name may be absent from the matriculation list if the institution has not forwarded the candidate’s verified matriculation details to the board. “Your institution admission office has not forwarded your verified matriculation details to JAMB,” the board said. It therefore advised affected candidates to contact their institutions and ensure their admissions are properly processed through the Central Admissions Processing System, known as JAMB CAPS. The third reason identified by the board is failure to print the JAMB original result slip and admission letter. “You have not printed your JAMB original results slip and admission letter,” JAMB said. The board advised candidates in this category to visit the nearest JAMB office or an approved Computer-Based Test centre to print the required documents. “So visit the nearest JAMB office or approved CBT centre and get it printed,” it advised. JAMB urged candidates to follow its official social media platforms for further updates and guidance on the matriculation list. Vanguard News The post JAMB lists 3 reasons candidates miss out on matriculation list appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Meta set to charge WhatsApp Business messages from October
items.description: Businesses using Meta’s WhatsApp Business Platform will begin paying for certain messages sent to customers from October 1, 2026, under a new pricing structure announced by the company. The change applies to organisations that use the WhatsApp Business Platform, formerly known as the WhatsApp Business API, to manage customer communication on a large scale. Regular WhatsApp users and small businesses using the standard WhatsApp Business app are not the main targets of the new charges. Under the revised system, the amount businesses pay will depend on the type of message being sent. Utility messages, including payment alerts, order confirmations and other service-related updates, will cost about $0.0101 per message, while marketing messages will attract a higher fee of approximately $0.062 each. Although the individual charges appear relatively small, companies that send large volumes of messages could see their communication expenses rise significantly. For example, a Nigerian fintech company sending 500,000 chargeable utility messages could incur about $5,050 in fees from Meta alone, excluding charges that may come from third-party providers or software platforms used to manage the messaging service. The development is particularly significant for Nigerian businesses, as banks, fintech companies, retailers, airlines and telecommunications firms increasingly rely on WhatsApp to communicate with customers. Banks and fintechs commonly use the platform for transaction notifications and account updates, while retailers use it for orders, enquiries and customer support. Airlines and telecom companies also rely on WhatsApp for routine service-related interactions. Small businesses and startups that depend on WhatsApp for both sales and customer service may also have to reconsider how they use the platform once the charges take effect. The new pricing model means businesses could be forced to identify essential messages, reduce unnecessary communication and closely monitor the cost of customer interactions through WhatsApp. Meta’s latest move follows an earlier shift in its business messaging model. In July 2025, the company moved away from its previous conversation-based pricing system for business-initiated template messages and adopted per-message billing. The October 2026 changes will further expand that approach by removing some of the free allowances previously available for service messages. For Nigerian companies that have built significant customer-service operations around WhatsApp, the change could turn the platform into a more substantial recurring business expense, potentially prompting some firms to explore alternative communication channels or adjust their messaging strategies. Attention, rien ne confirme l’arrestation de Mahmoud Dicko à Alger
items.description: Une publication devenue virale sur TikTok affirme que l'imam Mahmoud Dicko « a ete arrete a l'aeroport international Houari-Boumediene d'Alger, puis place en residence surveillee par les autorites algeriennes ». Aucune source officielle consultee par notre redaction ne confirme cette information. Depuis mardi 25 août, une publication largement relayee sur TikTok affirme que l'imam Mahmoud Dicko a ete « arrete a son arrivee a l'aeroport international Houari-Boumediene d'Alger ». Selon son auteur, l'imam aurait ensuite ete place en residence surveillee par les autorites algeriennes. La publication evoque egalement un possible « refoulement de l'imam vers le Mali ». La video comptabilisait plus de 137 000 vues et des milliers d'interactions au moment de notre verification. Ces chiffres peuvent toutefois evoluer rapidement. Aucune confirmation de l'arrestation Apres recherches, recoupements et verifications, aucune source officielle consultee ne confirme l'arrestation de Mahmoud Dicko a Alger. Notre redaction a egalement contacte plusieurs personnes proches de l'imam. Aucune n'a confirme son arrestation ni un eventuel placement en residence surveillee. a ce stade, rien ne permet donc d'affirmer que Mahmoud Dicko a ete arrete a Alger ou place en residence surveillee par les autorites algeriennes. Une information a prendre avec prudence Le nombre de vues ou d'interactions d'une publication sur les reseaux sociaux ne constitue pas une preuve de la veracite de l'information qu'elle diffuse. En l'absence de confirmation officielle ou de source fiable permettant d'etayer ces affirmations, cette publication doit etre prise avec des pincettes. Avant de partager une information virale, il est preferable d'en verifier l'origine et de rechercher une confirmation aupres de sources fiables. Lire aussi : Cette video ne montre pas une attaque du JNIM contre une station-service a Badalabougou L’article Attention, rien ne confirme l’arrestation de Mahmoud Dicko à Alger est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: ​ Axe AIBD-Dakar : la circulation totalement paralysée par un grave carambolage
items.description: Un spectaculaire carambolage impliquant plusieurs véhicules s'est produit ce vendredi 28 août sur l'autoroute à péage reliant l'Aéroport international Blaise Diagne (AIBD) à Dakar. L'accident a entraîné la fermeture complète du tronçon situé entre Toglou et Sébikotane, plongeant la zone dans une congestion majeure. Aux alentours de 11 h 30, les autorités sur place signalaient un embouteillage s'étirant sur près de 4 kilomètres. La gravité des collisions et l'ampleur du bouchon compliquent fortement la progression des équipes d'intervention et des secours. Face à cette paralysie du trafic, les services de régulation de la circulation invitent instamment les usagers en provenance de l'AIBD ou du réseau autoroutier Segea à emprunter la sortie n° 13 afin de contourner le secteur via la Route Nationale. Il est vivement conseillé aux automobilistes de faire preuve de vigilance et de différer ou d'anticiper l'ensemble de leurs déplacements dans la zone.

items.title: FCT emergency department rescues 2 from collapsed Kubwa building
items.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Emergency Management Department (FEMD) says it has rescued two from a collapsed building in Kubwa. The department’s Head of Media and Public Relations, Nkechi Isa, said this in a statement on Friday in Abuja. Isa said that the trapped ground-floor residents were rescued following a swift response to an 11:38 a.m distress call. She said that the one-storey residential structure, comprising six blocks of flats located at Kubwa 2/2 by Yellow Page, partially caved in at around 11:30 a.m on Friday. She said that emergency responders safely extracted both victims from the rubble of the building’s collapsed right segment. ​”Other tenants were out for the day when the incident occurred, preventing further casualties, though household items and property were destroyed. “The two rescued victims were immediately rushed to the Kubwa General Hospital, where officials confirmed that they were in stable condition. ​”The Department of Development Control and the FCT Police Command joined FEMD at the scene to secure the area and investigate the cause of the structural failure,” she said.
