items.title: Pims fire: Mustafa Kamal says 'no one will be spared', calls for reforming health sector
items.description: Minister for National Health Services Regulation and Coordination Mustafa Kamal on Friday vowed that “no one will be spared” while talking about the fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) that claimed the lives of 14 infants, adding that the country’s health sector needed to be reformed. Speaking in the Senate, Kamal said: “No one intends to spare or save anyone. I am saying this on behalf of the prime minister and the entire government that not a single person will be spared”. He said that the tragedy cannot be an “episode lasting merely a few days,” as he called for accountability and for efforts to prevent such incidents in the future. The minister warned against “suppressing the issue” and invited the House to work towards a way forward, agreeing to a proposal seeking the formation of a parliamentary committee comprising opposition members to investigate Wednesday’s incident. “Look at your resources, management and actions and then involve everyone to suggest a way forward,” he said, assuring that the government will support such an approach. “This is a matter of children’s lives, and we are answerable to God for it. The ministry is nothing; we cannot ruin our afterlife for these ministries,” he remarked. At the outset of his address, the minister expressed sorrow at the lives lost in the incident. “There can be no explanation for this. I am holding myself responsible, and I have presented myself to be held accountable.” He called for a holistic approach toward investigating the incident, urging that any committee formed to probe should not be “time-bound and should remain open”. “When you go investigate this incident, you will find so many things associated with it,” he said, pointing to a larger “rot” within the sector. Kamal held that the health sector was not “ideal”. “Four hundred thousand children between the ages of one and five die every year, 1,300 die every day; they are all dying preventable deaths,” he said. He continued: “It is not possible to bring back the infants who died at Pims, but let us look at it as a test from God and prevent the next kid from dying.” Kamal maintained that there was “no point” in making speeches if the government failed to learn from the incident. “Start from me,” Kamal said, offering himself up for accountability. “Sit with us and save the next from dying. I am putting the entire ministry at your disposal; every person will be answerable to you,” he said. He noted that the system was “rotten” and went on to say: “Where do I find a better person after removing an incompetent one?” Kamal said that when the day ended, “1,300 children would have died across the country”. Speaking about the inquiry committee’s report on the incident, which he said would be presented by tonight, Kamal assured the House: “If you don’t trust it, fair enough [..] we will listen to you.” The health minister once again reassured the House that, “No one will be spared, no matter how influential they are”. “We have to come up with a solution, and I am inviting you to guide us and [..] give us a strategic roadmap,” he said. Kamal said that the health ministry would provide all the relevant input and information. “Sit with us and find a way forward on how to prevent the next child from dying due to negligence within the resources that we have. I assure you of its implementation”. However, he added that if matters were to move in that direction, “no MNA should call and ask why a certain doctor was removed”. Calling for “radical reforms” in the health sector, Kamal urged that the Pims fire “can serve as a basis for how we can prevent more children from dying”. The minister further stated that he was “withholding his information” on the fire until the committee’s report. “If you are dissatisfied (with the report), then form a committee, and everyone stands ready to be held accountable”. Concluding his address, Kamal urged that the “issue should be only closed at a point where we can prevent similar incidents in the future”. “I am willing to sit here all night and listen,” he added. The minister, during his address, in response to calls for his resignation, said: “Let the investigation be completed. I have already taken action beyond what they are thinking.” Sherry Rehman calls for accountability; PTI’s Ali Zafar proposes formation of committee The routine business in the Senate was suspended on a motion moved by PPP parliamentary leader in the House Senator Sherry Rehman for a thorough discussion on the Pims fire. Speaking in the Senate, Rehman stressed that the incident raised serious questions of governance, accountability and public safety. “Wherever there is a failure, there must be accountability. Audit and accountability are an integral part of politics. Working for public interest in the Senate is politics. Politics is to work for the good of people, to work for public interest. Politics is all about accountability.“ she stressed. Rehman said her concerns were also rooted in her own experience as a former health minister. “I have served as health minister for six months. I was also given reasons to close the emergency gates, but I did not. Instead, I posted guards there and checked myself. Why are incompetent people who don’t care about basic safety protocols even allowed to continue?” “The executive director of Pims was lying when he said that the emergency gate was not closed. The firefighters and the Capital Development Authority (CDA) have stated that the gate was closed. What is the purpose of an emergency exit? It is supposed to remain open for emergencies,” Rehman questioned. Rehman also pointed to contradictions between the Pims report and the findings of CDA, particularly concerning the hospital’s fire-safety arrangements. “The PIMS report contradicts the CDA’s findings. The CDA has repeatedly stated that the hospital’s fire-safety arrangements are inadequate. Why was no notice taken? The hospital does not even have a fire NOC.” Senator Rehman highlighted the substantial federal funding provided to Pims, and questioned why basic safety standards had not been ensured despite the availability of resources. PTI leader Barrister Ali Zafar proposed the formation of a special committee comprising an equal number of government and opposition members, with an opposition member as its head. He said the committee should examine hospital safety and emergency preparedness and develop comprehensive Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for dealing with foreseeable hazards and emergencies. The committee, he proposed, should also ensure that these SOPs are available, properly implemented and regularly reviewed in every hospital “Let us start with Islamabad,” he said. Zafar further proposed that the committee be empowered to inspect hospitals, call for records, seek explanations from hospital administrations and co-opt medical, fire-safety, engineering, disaster-management and other relevant experts whenever required. He said the administrations of all hospitals should be directed to fully cooperate with the committee and provide all necessary information, records, facilities and assistance required for it to perform its mandate. “This should not be another committee that merely produces a report which sits on a shelf,” he said. According to Zafar, the committee should be focused on identifying failures, correcting them, establishing enforceable safety protocols and ensuring compliance. “We owe this not only to those who lost their lives in this tragedy, but to every patient and every family who will have to depend on our hospitals in the future,” he said. The Senate also passed unanimously a resolution calling for the formation of a special Senate committee to investigate the incident on Friday. It was moved by Senator Rehman. NA passes resolution for inquiry into fire Meanwhile, the National Assembly unanimously approved a resolution, calling for an impartial inquiry into the incident and expressing condolences to the affected families. Through the resolution, a copy of which is available with Dawn , lawmakers expressed “profound grief and sorrow” over the incident and strongly condemned it. They raised alarm at the circumstances surrounding the fire, with the resolution stating that the circumstances were a result of “sheer negligence”. It called upon the government to “take strict action against anyone responsible for negligence or safety lapses in accordance with the law”. Lawmakers also called on the government to ensure that fire safety and emergency preparedness measures were strictly implemented in federal government hospitals, particularly in neonatal and paediatric units, to prevent such incidents in the future. “The House […] extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and prays for strength and fortitude for them in this hour of profound grief,” the resolution added. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar expressed his condolences and informed the NA about the steps taken by the prime minister. He said that PM Shehbaz had constituted two committees — one headed by Dr Azhar Kiani and the other by former Secretary Shahid Khan. The committee headed by Dr Kiani would provide information on what was required for the improvement of Pims. The minister also asked for concrete suggestions to be made in the House instead of the issue being politicised. Former prime minister and PPP leader Raja Pervez Ashraf said that the nation had a “habit” of forming a committee or a commission on such matters to keep it alive, but eventually forgetting about the incident within a few weeks. “We need to have a change of approach towards hazards and the health sector,” he said. Ashraf criticised that even after days, nobody was clear about the reasons for the accident, calling for a committee of parliamentarians belonging to all parties in the House to investigate the matter and “at least” inquire into the cause of the fire. PTI senior leader Asad Qaiser noted that the fateful incident occurred at the same hospital that the government claimed had the best facilities when it came to the treatment of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan. Last week, Imran had undergone a medical check-up at Pims — rather than Islamabad’s private Shifa International Hospital as per the directions of the Supreme Court — before being shifted back to Adiala jail. Rs5m compensation announced for affected families Earlier in the day, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry announced Rs5 million compensation for each family affected by the fire. Recalling Wednesday’s incident while speaking to the media at Pims, Chaudhry lamented that 14 infants had fallen victim to “someone’s criminal negligence”. He added that the prime minister had constituted an inquiry committee that was expected to present its report today, assuring that all those “on-duty individuals found guilty of negligence will be given exemplary punishment”. The minister said the grief of the affected families could not be compensated for. “Neither can their children be brought back, nor can their grief be reduced,” he added. “But to provide some relief […] the prime minister has announced that Rs5 million will be given to all the affected families.” Chaudhry said he was visiting Pims to hand over a cheque to one of the affected families on behalf of the prime minister, adding that the compensation amount would be deposited in the accounts of the deceased children’s mothers. “This is a small effort to share their sorrow,” he remarked. Responding to a question about demands for DNA tests of the bodies, he said most of the deceased children died in the incident not because they were burnt but because of suffocation due to smoke. “So all of them could be identified,” he said, adding that after birth, infants had tags with their mothers’ names on their arms. “So they were easily identified.” Deadly fire at Pims On Wednesday, 14 babies were killed after a fire erupted at the Mother and Child Healthcare Centre at Pims. According to a Pims statement, the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside the nursery at 06:38am”, and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator. It said two doctors and two nurses on duty responded immediately and called security staff, who tried twice to enter the nursery before a blast occurred and the ceilings collapsed. But, witnesses said they waited hours for emergency services and were forced to smash windows to reach the affected ward, while some alleged that doors were locked. The hospital and government later disputed claims of delays and locked emergency exits. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has formed a high-level inquiry committee to probe the incident and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri. The tragedy has since sparked widespread outrage and calls for accountability, with the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on National Health Services also demanding answers from the Pims administration over possible negligence and safety lapses.

items.title: Govt withdraws controversial telecom bill, to bring new draft of proposed legislation
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The government on Friday withdrew a controversial bill that sought to give telecom licensees sweeping powers to install infrastructure on public and private land , saying it would introduce a new draft of the proposed legislation. The bill, seeking changes to a 1996 act , was originally tabled by Shaza Fatima Khawaja and approved by the National Assembly on June 11 by a majority vote, a day before the presentation of the federal budget 2026-27. It was then taken up in the Senate, where objections were raised about its clauses. On Friday, a motion to withdraw the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was moved in the upper house of Parliament by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry on behalf of Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja. The motion was passed by the House as the stipulated 90-day period for the bill’s passage was nearing expiry. “Upon expiry of the prescribed period, the bill would have proceeded to a joint sitting of Parliament, the convening of which may not take place in the near future,” the Ministry of Information Technology said in a statement . “In order to avoid delays and expedite the legislative process, the ministry has decided to introduce a fresh bill, ensuring that the legislative process proceeds in a timely and effective manner, while retaining the essence of the proposed legislation,” it said. The bill’s statement of objects and reasons said amendments were needed for “swift and coordinated deployment of telecommunication infrastructure”. Highlighting the government’s rationale, Khawaja said last month that the existing legal framework did not meet the demands of modern technologies such as 5G. Under the now-withdrawn bill, no public authority was to demand any “charges, fees, rent, of any nature whatsoever” for access. If a public authority did not respond within 30 days of a licensee’s request, even after a reminder, approval was to be “deemed to have been granted”. For private land, licensees were to seek approval from owners/tenants by registered mail. No response in 30 days would allow the matter to be referred to the “appropriate government.” For housing societies, cooperative schemes and commercial estates, access was to be deemed approved after 30 days, though owners could impose conditions on timing and manner of work. “Disputes must be settled within 45 days by an officer not below the rank of secretary,” the bill said. It defined “private access” to include individual ownership and collective ownership by housing societies, Defence Housing Authority and cantonments. “Public authority” covered federal and provincial governments and local bodies. The bill also proposed fines of up to Rs50 million on any owner, tenant or entity that obstructed access. The clauses triggered a strong backlash , with critics calling them “draconian” and saying that they violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which protects property rights. The Islamabad Bar Association and digital rights groups warned the law could be used for “forced entry” into private premises. Several lawmakers, from both opposition and treasury benches, also raised concerns, while the PPP flat out refused to support the bill in the Senate. Following public criticism and media reports, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice and constituted a committee headed by Minister for Law and Justice Azam Nazeer Tarar to examine the legislation. Khawaja later clarified that the bill “would not allow anyone to occupy private land”. Officials said the new draft would retain right-of-way provisions for public infrastructure but make prior consent mandatory for private property. Officials said the amendments were aimed at removing right-of-way bottlenecks that have delayed fibre and 5G rollout in Pakistan. They said the nationwide rollout of modern telecommunications services required extensive infrastructure, including fibre-optic networks, telecom towers and both underground and overground installations. The number of fibre-based internet connections has increased from two million to over five million in the past two years, through various policy and technical interventions, and a target has been set to double this in the next three years. Telecom operators had lobbied for the law, citing months-long delays in getting no-objection certificates from cantonments, housing societies and provincial authorities.

items.title: What Dolly Parton Knew About Reading
items.description: This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. My best friend’s baby got mail from Dolly Parton on the day the singer died. This wasn’t unexpected: He’s been receiving books from Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library for all 10 months of his life. (This month’s selection was Bedtime, Here I Come , by D. J. Steinberg.) And he wasn’t alone—the Imagination Library sends free books to children every month from birth to age 5; the program has passed out more than 300 million books in five countries. My colleague Annie Joy Williams wrote earlier this week about the legacy of Parton —and her books program—in Tennessee, the home state that all three of us share. But the Imagination Library has expanded far beyond that territory. When I lived in an apartment building in Washington, D.C., I would see books bearing the library’s distinctive seal on a table in the lobby—volumes too big for my neighbor’s mailbox, quietly awaiting little hands. First, here are three new stories from The Atlantic ’s Books section: Portrait of the artist as a movie star “Tallying,” a poem by Joanna Klink “Wilderness Years,” a poem by Dave Lucas The progress that can’t be erased Stories about Parton’s generosity are spreading widely: She helped fund a COVID-19 vaccine and filmed herself getting the shot when many Americans were hesitant. She opened a sanctuary for bald eagles! She did so many things for so many kinds of Americans, and especially Tennesseans, that I find it hard to keep track. But she said, many times, that she’d be happy to be remembered not as a generational talent or a dolled-up diva but as “the book lady.” Parton grew up in poverty in East Tennessee, and she frequently cited her illiterate father as the inspiration for her books program, which she founded in 1995. I don’t know whether all of Parton’s fans knew how high she ranked literacy on her list of important causes, but when I watched tributes to Parton roll in this week, I noted that people I’d grown up with in Tennessee (mostly young women like me) kept posting the same tableaus on Instagram: photos of babies and kids sitting with their parents, reading a book they’d gotten from the Imagination Library. The photos are cute—but they also reflect something deeply important. A few years ago, I edited an essay by the children’s-book author Katherine Marsh that identified one reason young kids were less motivated to read: Schools often push them toward a “hyperfocus on analysis” and give precedence to individual paragraphs and sentences rather than entire narratives. But, Marsh argues, “the best way to present an abstract idea to kids is by hooking them on a story.” And a great way to get a kid interested in a story is by reading it aloud to them. In another article, published a year ago, Ilana Kurshan wrote about this declining but important practice , and about doing it with her son: “The delight of reading to him lay not in the pages we turned,” she wrote, “but in the wheels that seemed to turn in his mind as we read together.” Thanks to my friends’ beloved babies and the perks of my job— which have included putting together a list of essential children’s books —I’ve been thinking a lot about the importance of reading with children. They still encounter books in schools and libraries, but Parton’s program emphasized building a bookshelf at home, where caregivers and kids can share stories as part of a daily routine. Reading aloud offers a child more than the chance to develop literacy skills. It gave Kurshan, for example, “a way to guide them as they started to understand the world, and as I started to understand them.” So, like Parton, I’ll be happy if kids see me as a “book lady.” Last week, I bought a picture book about berries for a different toddler. And although my friend’s 10-month-old already has plenty at home, I couldn’t resist mailing him a few more books. Peter Marlow / Magnum What Parents Lose When They Don’t Read to Their Kids By Ilana Kurshan Sharing books with my children was about a lot more than literacy. Read the full article. What to Read Hippos Go Berserk! , by Sandra Boynton Hippos Go Berserk! , a sterling example of Boynton’s comedic genius, has the subtitle “A wild counting story.” “One hippo, all alone, calls two hippos on the phone,” it begins, and each page introduces another attendee to a gathering being planned in real time, until 45 of them crowd an all-night cocktail party. Then come the visual gags: There’s a hippo’s version of Whistler’s Mother , a hippo upside-down, and one guest, a classic spiky-furred grinning Boynton beastie, who consistently eludes the count. As the hippos gradually leave, little creature in tow, Berserk shows that even basic arithmetic can be an act of imagination, rather than rote repetition—and it cleverly reminds adult readers that the most familiar exercise can invite unexpected images into the mind. — Walt Hunter From our list: 65 essential children’s books Out Next Week 📚 The Castle: Adventures in a World of Unraveling Men , by Jon Ronson 📚 I Liked Rex , by Diane Williams 📚 All the Hidden Places , by Cadwell Turnbull Your Weekend Read The painter Milton Avery Arnold. Newman Properties / Getty The Painter Who Shaped Rothko By Sebastian Smee Beginning in the early 1930s, three Americans—Milton Avery, Mark Rothko, and Adolph Gottlieb—began spending summers together on Cape Ann, along the coast of northeast Massachusetts. They loved the gritty authenticity of Gloucester, the nation’s oldest fishing port. Cape Ann’s distinctive, undulant geography combined pungent industry and village intensity with Atlantic immensity of sea and sky. The story of the relationships among these artists, in particular between the older Avery and the now–stratospherically famous Rothko, shows us American modernism in its moment of greatest transition. Read the full article. When you buy a book using a link in this newsletter, we receive a commission. Thank you for supporting The Atlantic . items.title: Rentrée scolaire : Le ministère impose un suivi quotidien des absences dès le 7 septembre
items.description: À quelques jours de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, le ministère de l’Éducation nationale, du Préscolaire et des Sports resserre son dispositif de suivi afin de garantir un démarrage effectif des cours dès le lundi 7 septembre. Au-delà de l’organisation pédagogique, l’administration entend surveiller de près la présence des élèves et l’approvisionnement du marché en manuels et fournitures scolaires. Dans une note adressée aux directeurs des Académies régionales de l’éducation et de la formation ainsi qu’aux responsables provinciaux, le ministère rappelle que le 7 septembre constitue la date officielle du début effectif et obligatoire des enseignements pour l’ensemble des cycles et niveaux scolaires. À partir de cette échéance, les établissements sont tenus de lancer les activités pédagogiques conformément aux emplois du temps arrêtés, sans différer le démarrage des cours en raison d’éventuels retards d’inscription de certains élèves. Cette instruction s’inscrit dans le calendrier déjà annoncé par le département de tutelle, qui prévoit un accueil progressif des élèves entre le 3 et le 5 septembre, selon les niveaux d’enseignement, avant la généralisation des cours à l’ensemble des établissements du Royaume le 7 septembre. Le ministère insiste également sur un principe qu’il juge essentiel : l’accès à l’école ne doit en aucun cas être conditionné au paiement des frais d’inscription. La note, signée par le secrétaire général du département, rappelle ainsi aux responsables éducatifs l’obligation de permettre à chaque élève de rejoindre sa classe dès le début de l’année scolaire, indépendamment de sa situation administrative ou financière. L’accent est par ailleurs mis sur le suivi de l’assiduité. Les établissements sont appelés à enregistrer les absences dès le premier jour de cours et à alimenter régulièrement les systèmes d’information relatifs à la fréquentation scolaire. L’objectif est d’obtenir rapidement une photographie précise des taux de présence et d’identifier les situations de retard ou de risque de décrochage. Le dispositif de remontée des données repose sur une organisation à plusieurs niveaux. Les directions provinciales seront chargées de centraliser les informations transmises par les établissements et d’en produire des synthèses, tandis que les Académies régionales devront consolider les données à l’échelle territoriale avant leur transmission à la Direction générale de l’action pédagogique. Selon le ministère, cette architecture de suivi doit permettre à l’administration centrale de disposer d’une vision détaillée du déroulement de la rentrée, d’identifier les établissements ou les zones accusant des retards dans l’arrivée des élèves et d’intervenir rapidement lorsque la situation l’exige. Cette vigilance s’accompagnera d’un effort accru de communication avec les familles et les associations de parents d’élèves. Parallèlement au contrôle de la présence scolaire, le ministère engage une opération spécifique consacrée à la disponibilité des manuels et fournitures scolaires. Des cellules de suivi seront mises en place au niveau provincial afin d’évaluer l’état de l’approvisionnement dans les différents points de vente relevant du ressort de chaque direction. À partir du vendredi 28 août, des visites de terrain devront être effectuées dans les librairies afin de vérifier la disponibilité des ouvrages prescrits pour les différents niveaux d’enseignement et de signaler toute pénurie ou tout retard de distribution. La note prévoit également la tenue d’au moins deux réunions hebdomadaires sous la présidence des directeurs provinciaux. Ces rencontres auront pour objectif d’exploiter les résultats des opérations de contrôle, de dresser un état des dysfonctionnements constatés et de définir les mesures correctives à mettre en œuvre, notamment dans les territoires où certains manuels ou fournitures viendraient à manquer. Le ministère demande en outre un renforcement de la coordination avec les services des wilayas et des préfectures, en particulier les départements chargés des affaires économiques et de la coordination. Cette collaboration doit permettre de suivre l’approvisionnement des librairies, d’anticiper les difficultés susceptibles de perturber le marché et d’assurer une disponibilité suffisante des fournitures scolaires. Les associations de parents d’élèves sont également invitées à participer aux opérations de suivi et de sensibilisation. À l’échelle régionale, les Académies sont chargées de coordonner l’ensemble du dispositif et de maintenir un contact permanent avec la cellule centrale d’appui, d’accompagnement et de veille. L’objectif est de signaler rapidement les situations de pénurie et de corriger les éventuels dysfonctionnements avant qu’ils n’affectent le déroulement normal de l’année scolaire. Par ces mesures, le ministère entend sécuriser les conditions de la rentrée 2026-2027 et garantir, dès les premiers jours de septembre, le respect du temps scolaire et du temps d’apprentissage dans l’ensemble des établissements du pays. The post Rentrée scolaire : Le ministère impose un suivi quotidien des absences dès le 7 septembre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Four plead guilty to London arson attack on Jewish ambulances
items.description: Four young men admitted on Friday being behind an arson attack on London ambulances owned by a Jewish charity at a UK court hearing. British nationals Hamza Iqbal, 20, Rehan Khan, 19, Judex Atshatshi, 18, and British-Pakistani Saif Ali, 18, all pleaded guilty to criminal damage linked to the March 23 attack. Four ambulances run by the Hatzola charity were destroyed in a London neighbourhood home to a signficant Jewish population, one of a spate of attacks in the British capital targeting Jewish or Israel-linked locations.

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca termine en territoire négatif
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a terminé dans le rouge vendredi, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,61% à 18.931,06 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a diminué de 0,28% à 1.358,68 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a reculé de 0,87% à 1.409,94 pts. De son côté, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a lâché 0,07% à 1.815,12 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Sylviculture et papier » (-2,61%), « Mines » (-1,98%) et « Société de financement et autres activités financières » (-1,74%) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Industrie agricole » (+2,5%), « Électricité » (+1,11%) et « Ingénieries et biens d'équipement industriels » (+1,11%) ont signé les meilleures performances. Les échanges ont dépassé 580,1 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central et dominés par les transactions sur Attijariwafa Bank (288,84 MDH), Managem (63,32 MDH) et Itissalat Al-Maghrib (39,72 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est, quant à elle, établie à plus de 1.118,19 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes baisses ont été accusées par Rebab Company (-4,76% à 100 DH), Cash Plus S.A (-3,43% à 245,2 DH), Fenie Brossette (-3,23% à 392 DH), Atlantasanad (-3,01% à 124,15 DH) et SMI (-2,82% à 6.900 DH). En revanche, Promopharm S.A. (+5,97% à 1.296 DH), Maghrebail (+3,37% à 916,9 DH), Involys (+3,06% à 132,95 DH), Zellidja S.A (+3% à 319,8 DH) et Aluminium du Maroc (+2,87% à 1.901 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes hausses. The post La Bourse de Casablanca termine en territoire négatif appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: AES : La jeunesse appelée à promouvoir la paix, la discipline et le patriotisme
items.description: Burkina-Rencontre-Jeunesse-AES AES : La jeunesse appelée à promouvoir la paix, la discipline et le patriotisme Ouagadougou, 28 août 2026 (AIB) – Le président des Sessions confédérales des Parlements de l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel (AES), Dr Ousmane Bougouma, a appelé vendredi à Ouagadougou, la jeunesse de l’espace confédéral à promouvoir les valeurs de paix, de discipline, de travail bien fait, de solidarité et de patriotisme, à l’ouverture du Forum confédéral de la jeunesse et du volontariat 2026. « Vous avez la responsabilité de promouvoir les valeurs de paix, de discipline, de travail bien fait, de solidarité, de patriotisme et de respect de l’intérêt général, qui constituent le socle de nos réalités sociales et culturelles », a déclaré Dr Ousmane Bougouma, dans un discours lu par le premier vice-président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), David D. Lompo. Le président des Sessions confédérales des Parlements de l’AES a également exhorté les jeunes à combattre les discours de haine, les manipulations, la désinformation et toutes les formes de division susceptibles de fragiliser les sociétés de l’espace confédéral. Il les a, par ailleurs, invités à traduire leur engagement en initiatives concrètes en faveur du développement local, du volontariat, de la participation citoyenne et de la cohésion sociale. Pour Dr Bougouma, le forum ne doit pas être « une simple rencontre de circonstance », mais plutôt une tribune permettant de faire émerger des idées novatrices et des actions concrètes. « J’attends de vos travaux des propositions ambitieuses, réalistes et opérationnelles, susceptibles d’éclairer les décisions de nos gouvernements et des institutions de la Confédération », a-t-il indiqué. Il s’est dit convaincu que les recommandations issues des travaux contribueront à renforcer la coopération entre les Etats de l’AES, à promouvoir la mobilité des jeunes dans l’espace confédéral, à développer les partenariats économiques et culturels et à accélérer la mise en œuvre de politiques communes répondant aux aspirations de la jeunesse. La ministre burkinabè des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi, Annick Pikbougoum Zingué/Ouattara, a estimé que le forum constitue une étape importante dans la construction politique et citoyenne de l’espace confédéral, fondée sur l’engagement et la responsabilité de la jeunesse. Elle a relevé plusieurs attentes à l’endroit des jeunes, notamment la consolidation de la cohésion entre les peuples à travers le dialogue, le respect et la solidarité, la promotion de la paix, le renforcement de la résilience des communautés et la lutte contre la violence, la haine et la désinformation. La ministre a également appelée la jeunesse à soutenir l’innovation, l’entrepreneuriat, la formation et l’emploi et à porter une vision commune fondée sur des valeurs partagées. « La jeunesse doit donc être à la fois une force sociale, civique et citoyenne », a-t-elle soutenu. La ministre chargée de la jeunesse a invité les jeunes à prendre des engagements concrets, réalistes et applicables, à participer à la mise en œuvre des projets confédéraux à fort impact et à contribuer à la mise en place de mécanismes de coordination en faveur de la jeunesse et du volontariat. Pour le ministre malien chargé de la Jeunesse, Abdoul Kassim Ibrahim Fomba, la vision des dirigeants de l’espace confédéral vis-à-vis de la jeunesse est claire : elle doit consacrer son énergie au service de sa communauté, de son pays et de l’espace confédéral. Son homologue nigérien, Sidi Mohamed Almahmoud, a, quant à lui, appelé les jeunes des trois pays à renforcer leur solidarité, rappelant que les Etats de l’AES sont « frères ». Selon lui, cette fraternité ne doit pas se limiter aux discours, mais doit se traduire par des actions concrètes, des projets communs et une solidarité agissante. « Le forum est un cadre privilégié pour faire émerger cette dynamique », a-t-il conclu. Le Forum confédéral de la jeunesse et du volontariat des Etats du Sahel se tient du 28 au 30 août 2026 à Ouagadougou sous le thème : « Consolidation de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES) : rôle, responsabilité et engagement de la jeunesse ». La rencontre réunit des jeunes venus du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger ainsi que de pays frères. Agence d’information du Burkina DNK/yos

items.title: Bam : plus de 340 Appelés s’engagent à ne jamais trahir le Burkina Faso
items.description: Bam : plus de 340 Appelés s’engagent à ne jamais trahir le Burkina Faso Kongoussi, 27 août 2026 (AIB)-Plus de 340 jeunes Appelés à l’immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) de la province du Bam se sont engagés, jeudi à Kongoussi, à ne jamais trahir le Burkina Faso, lors de leur cérémonie officielle de sortie présidée par haut-commissaire de la province, Karim Ouédraogo au lycée municipal polyvalent de Kongoussi. C’est en présence des responsables du commandement militaire et paramilitaire, des parents, des responsables d’établissements et des forces vives de la province que les appelés ont solennellement réaffirmé leur attachement à leur patrie et pris l’engagement de rester fidèles au Burkina Faso, leur pays natal. Cet engagement intervient au terme d’une formation qui a permis de renforcer leur patriotisme, leur civisme et leur sens de la responsabilité citoyenne. Le porte-parole et délégué de la promotion, Abdoul Razak Zougouri, a exprimé sa reconnaissance à l’encadrement militaire et civil pour les enseignements reçus durant le mois. Il a expliqué que cette immersion leur a permis d’acquérir des connaissances en matière de patriotisme, de civisme, de vivre-ensemble et de cohésion sociale. Les jeunes bacheliers ont également été initiés à la self-défense et au secourisme. « Nous remercions les autorités et l’ensemble de nos encadreurs, de nos parents et de nos enseignants grâce à qui nous avons bénéficié de cette formation. Nous leur disons merci et prenons l’engagement de ne jamais trahir le Burkina Faso, notre pays », a-t-il déclaré. Le haut-commissaire du Bam, Karim Ouédraogo, par ailleurs président de la cellule provinciale de coordination de l’immersion patriotique obligatoire a pour sa part invité les jeunes à traduire cet engagement patriotique dans leurs comportements quotidiens. « Le patriotisme ne se résume ni aux discours, ni aux chants, ni au port d’un uniforme. Le véritable patriotisme se manifeste dans vos comportements quotidiens », a-t-il déclaré. Il a exhorté les appelés à respecter les lois, à protéger les biens publics, à travailler avec honnêteté et à contribuer à la paix et à la cohésion sociale. « Je vous invite à faire de la discipline votre boussole, du travail votre moteur, de l’engagement votre élan et de la solidarité votre force », a-t-il poursuivi. Karim Ouédraogo les a également appelés à faire preuve de discernement sur les réseaux sociaux et à éviter de contribuer à la propagation de la haine et de la désinformation. La cérémonie a pris fin par une démonstration de self-défense et de secourisme et d’un défilé des appelés. Agence d’information du Burkina AR/ata

items.title: Guinée : une délégation ivoirienne de la BSTP en immersion chez MADI-GROUP, le projet Vill’Harmonia au cœur de la visite
items.description: Une délégation de la Bourse de sous-traitance et de partenariat de Côte d’Ivoire (BSTP-CI) a effectué, ce jeudi 27 août 2026, une visite d’immersion au sein de MADI-GROUP, à Ansoumania, dans la périphérie de Conakry. Cette étape, organisée dans le cadre d’une mission d’étude en Guinée, a notamment permis aux visiteurs de découvrir les activités d’Easy Logistics ainsi que le projet immobilier Vill’Harmonia, développé sur une superficie de 127 hectares. 0-3840×2160-0-0-{}-0-24# La mission ivoirienne, conduite par le directeur général de la BSTP Côte d’Ivoire, Amaël Konaté, séjourne en Guinée dans le cadre d’un voyage d’étude sous-régional organisé du 24 au 28 août 2026, avec l’appui de la GIZ et de la Direction du contenu local. Elle est accueillie par la BSTP Guinée et accompagnée notamment de représentants de la Direction générale du contenu local (DGCL) et du Guichet unique du contenu local (GPMCI). La visite a commencé par une immersion dans les activités d’Easy Logistics. Cette filiale intervient notamment dans le transport d’hydrocarbures, la logistique minière et BTP ainsi que la supervision télématique de sa flotte. L’entreprise indique disposer d’une flotte de citernes conformes aux normes ADR/OICMF pour le transport sécurisé de carburants, LFO, HFO et lubrifiants. Elle affirme également avoir mis en place une supervision télématique permanente, avec une flotte géolocalisée et équipée de caméras embarquées. MADI-GROUP fait par ailleurs état d’un système de management certifié autour d’un objectif « zéro accident ». Vill’Harmonia, un projet de 127 hectares Après cette immersion dans les activités logistiques, la délégation s’est rendue sur le chantier de Vill’Harmonia, à Ansoumania. Porté par sa filiale de promotion immobilière B2D Immobilier, le projet de MADI-GROUP s’étend sur 127 hectares et mobilise l'expertise de plusieurs entités du groupe, dont Easy Immo et Easy Logistics. Présentant les caractéristiques techniques du projet, Mamadou Diallo, ingénieur chez Easy Immo pour le compte de B2D Immobilier, explique que les études relatives aux voiries et réseaux divers (VRD) ont déjà été réalisées. « C'est un projet de 127 hectares sur l'ensemble de Vill’Harmonia. Toutes les études de VRD ont été faites sur le site. À part ces études de voiries et réseaux divers, nous avons aussi le certificat de conformité », a-t-il indiqué. Le projet est subdivisé en zones résidentielle et commerciale. Dans la partie résidentielle, des duplex de type R+1 sont prévus, tandis que la zone commerciale devrait notamment accueillir des immeubles allant jusqu’à R+4. Trois catégories d'habitations sont proposées. Les « Phaetons », présentés comme des logements de haut standing, disposent d'une surface bâtie de 315 m² sur des parcelles de 500 m². Les « Ibis » offrent 240 m² bâtis sur des terrains de 300 m². Enfin, les « Calao », destinés notamment aux coopératives, sont conçus sur des parcelles de 250 m², pour une surface bâtie de 200 m². La gestion des eaux au centre de la conception L'ingénieur a également insisté sur la gestion des eaux et le risque d'inondation dans cette zone située à proximité d'un bras de mer. À l'en croire, les aménagements hydrauliques ont été conçus de façon à préserver la circulation naturelle de l'eau entre le site et la mer. « Pour le moment, nous n'avons pas d'inondation », a déclaré Mamadou Diallo, qui attribue cette situation aux études de VRD et aux caniveaux aménagés sur le site. Selon ses explications, ces ouvrages permettent à l'eau de circuler lors des mouvements de marée, sans obstruer son passage naturel. Les responsables du projet disent également avoir pris en compte l'existence d'anciennes digues aménagées par les riverains pour leurs activités agricoles. Concernant la construction des habitations, B2D Immobilier entend laisser une certaine latitude aux acquéreurs. Un client peut confier la réalisation de son logement aux entreprises du groupe ou choisir un autre constructeur. Dans ce dernier cas, les plans doivent toutefois être examinés afin de vérifier leur conformité avec les prescriptions du projet. À terme, quatre entrées sont prévues pour desservir Vill’Harmonia. Chacune devrait disposer d'un poste de sécurité, dans le cadre du dispositif de contrôle et de sécurisation annoncé par le promoteur. La BSTP ivoirienne salue « un modèle » de contenu local Au terme de la visite, le directeur général de la BSTP Côte d'Ivoire n'a pas caché sa satisfaction. Amaël Konaté explique que la mission vise avant tout à comprendre le fonctionnement de la BSTP Guinée et le modèle guinéen de contenu local, mais aussi à observer directement les entreprises locales qui doivent donner corps à cette politique. « Cette visite d'immersion ne peut pas s'effectuer sans que nous soyons en contact avec les entreprises du pays, pour voir leur manière de travailler, dans quel cadre elles travaillent et selon quelles normes », a-t-il expliqué. Après plusieurs visites effectuées au cours de son séjour, le responsable ivoirien dit avoir été particulièrement marqué par l'organisation observée au sein de MADI-GROUP. Même si la délégation n'a pas visité toutes les filiales du groupe, elle a pu découvrir celles intervenant dans la construction et la logistique. « Nous avons été totalement satisfaits par l'organisation mise en place par les équipes », a-t-il affirmé. Pour Amaël Konaté, l'expérience observée à Ansoumania illustre surtout l'importance du développement des compétences nationales dans la mise en œuvre des politiques de contenu local. « Le contenu local n'existe pas s'il n'y a pas de compétences », a-t-il insisté. Le directeur général de la BSTP Côte d'Ivoire estime même que l'entreprise peut être recommandée à des donneurs d'ordre guinéens comme étrangers. « On peut conseiller cette entreprise à n'importe quel donneur d'ordre […] simplement parce qu'elle sait ce qu'elle fait, elle sait où elle va et elle a une vision bien définie », a-t-il soutenu. Il a également salué le rôle du PDG de MADI-GROUP, Aliou Dieng, et l'adhésion des équipes à la vision portée par la direction du groupe. Pour le responsable ivoirien, l'organisation découverte en Guinée constitue une expérience susceptible d'inspirer d'autres pays de la sous-région. « Nous pensons que c'est même un exemple à répliquer au niveau de nos différents États, en Côte d'Ivoire, mais également en Afrique de l'Ouest », a conclu Amaël Konaté. La visite d'Ansoumania s'inscrit ainsi dans une démarche de partage d'expériences entre les structures guinéenne et ivoirienne chargées de promouvoir la sous-traitance et le contenu local, avec en toile de fond la question de la capacité des entreprises nationales à répondre aux exigences des grands décideurs.

items.title: The AI Backlash Gets Professional
items.description: I f there’s one thing America seems to agree on, it’s AI. Some three-quarters of Americans oppose a data center being built in their area, three-quarters of Americans think AI will hurt their job security, nearly 70 percent think the technology is advancing too quickly—the polls go on. Progressive and Republican candidates alike are bashing the tech industry to win primary elections. States and cities are halting plans for data-center development. Yet in cloistered San Francisco, where I live, staffers at OpenAI and Anthropic are developing this same feared technology at light speed and pulling down compensation packages that stretch to considerably more than $1 million. Silicon Valley’s growth is largely unencumbered by regulation, and President Trump’s administration has if anything used its authority to speed the AI industry along. The divide between these camps—the majority of people in this country who simply have to deal with the technology as it’s rolled out, and the much smaller population of people with direct influence over it—is a defining feature of this era. And so I noticed when a small group, with ties to both the Bay Area and Washington, started making noise, insisting that the AI race slow down and the technology be overseen not by executives and engineers, but by the broadest population possible. The group—which formally launched today and calls itself Irreplaceable, as in people are irreplaceable by machines —has an audacious and perhaps naive vision. It is essentially a protest against capitalism as it is practiced in America today, focused on resisting first and developing a coherent plan for the future later. I have seen exactly how bulletproof the AI companies are—pilfering seemingly infinite volumes of media to train their models, building unpermitted power plants for their data centers, and unleashing autonomous agents capable of massive security breaches, almost entirely without consequence . I wanted to meet with Irreplaceable’s founders to ask: How do they possibly expect to pull this off? [ Read: It may be time to panic about AI ] The organization is staffed with people who made a name for themselves in the climate movement, and they are hoping to avoid past mistakes by focusing on the emotional reaction Americans are having to AI, rather than anchoring their work in white papers and policy recommendations. “People get it,” Jeremy Ornstein—a campaign strategist for Irreplaceable and former organizer with the Sunrise Movement—told me. “People have the intuition that if we create machines more powerful than people, that could go dangerously and terribly wrong.” Phil Aroneanu, Irreplaceable’s executive director and a co-founder of the climate organization 350.org , told me he believes that climate advocates initially floundered because they acted as policy wonks. They thought that making evidence-based arguments about the dangers of melting ice sheets and rising sea levels to receptive congresspeople would be enough to pass nationwide climate legislation. Today, Aroneanu said, movements are built not necessarily on what people think, but instead on what they feel. For climate, that meant fossil-fuel-divestment campaigns, protesting oil pipelines, and the school strikes led by Greta Thunberg. People are already “feeling the squeeze,” Aroneanu told me. “And we should be pointing that anxiety and that anger in the right direction.” Irreplaceable will prioritize a range of issues: mitigating automation’s effects on the economy, protecting against government and corporate use of AI to surveil Americans, and establishing industry oversight and guardrails to prevent catastrophic disasters, such as widespread blackouts caused by AI-powered hacking or bot-engineered pandemics. As I spoke with the activists, I kept thinking about what had become of the climate movement—the Green New Deal passed, but only after being watered down, and it was then gutted by the second Trump administration—but their populist approach makes sense. Some of the biggest and perhaps only lasting successes over the past 15 years of American politics—the Tea Party, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, MAGA, and election denialism—have been fueled by outrage over an unfair economy and seemingly rigged politics. These organizers have demonstrated their ability to win significant battles. Sunrise, 350.org, and others were instrumental in passing national legislation, galvanizing widespread climate demonstrations, and accelerating private-sector development of renewable energy. And Irreplacable’s members have already flexed some muscle when it comes to AI. In July, hundreds of people gathered for what was likely the largest anti-AI demonstration in San Francisco’s history, marching from OpenAI’s headquarters to Anthropic’s and finally to Google’s. A few months earlier, some of these “Stop the AI Race” organizers had staged a somewhat disorganized protest: Attendees at times struggled to chant in unison. The second time around, the march was advised by Ornstein, and attendees had chant sheets, a marching band, and a slushy truck (to “freeze” AI). Already, a number of climate-oriented groups (including the environmental-justice arm of the NAACP as well as the Sierra Club and Earthjustice) are supporting local data-center battles by filing lawsuits, shaping model legislation, and organizing protests. The overlap is both concrete—data centers pollute the air and burn fossil fuels for their tremendous electricity demands—and thematic: a movement against corporate interests to change or regulate the technology of the future. At least on a local level, the groups are finding victories: Dozens of data centers have been canceled in the face of local opposition, and all of the major AI companies have promised to pay extra to avoid hiking up local electricity bills. In Michigan, both Abdul El-Sayed and William Lawrence, who is a co-founder of Sunrise, won Democratic primaries as progressive candidates hammering against data centers. Still, this bubbling AI anxiety is far from a sweeping tide. That growing numbers of Americans are concerned about AI development does not mean they are concerned for similar or even compatible reasons. People may say they loathe data centers, but they might also enjoy the conveniences of AI products at home or work. They fear bots getting too powerful, too quickly, but also think America needs to stay ahead of China in AI development. At one anti-AI protest, I saw people who were ostensibly on the same side disagree about AI’s water use and whether certain jobs would be better off automated by chatbots. And to the extent that a sufficiently powerful AI movement would need to be global, just as climate organizing was, the technology generally polls much better outside the U.S. The AI backlash is to some extent an American phenomenon, which bodes poorly for any sort of global norms or treaties. [ From the April 2026 issue: Inside the dirty, dystopian world of AI data centers ] When pressed, nobody from Irreplaceable and no other climate activists turning to AI would articulate a concrete AI agenda. “We’ve aligned around saying no,” Lawrence recently told me. “Now, there is an important conversation that is yet to come, about— okay, so what do we want? ” This is, for now, a significant weakness; a key turning point for the climate movement was providing a positive vision, the Green New Deal, for both decarbonizing and reinvigorating the American economy. Being able to link every data-center battle and primary campaign to a national vision would give the AI backlash some form. It’s not wrong to want to develop a policy road map with the input of a broad coalition; climate advocates took decades to devise and unite around the Green New Deal. Irreplaceable’s stated plan is to build a coalition this year, develop a unified policy next year, and implement that agenda by the end of 2029. Measured against any metric other than Silicon Valley’s warp speed, that would be fast. But those few years will leave plenty of time for tech companies to push back—they’ve already spent tens of millions of dollars leading up to the midterms—and regardless, by then OpenAI, Anthropic, and any number of Chinese firms may already have built and lost control of even more powerful models. Irreplaceable is wagering that people can move faster than capital. Absent specific policies, they are basically placing a big bet on populism—that the issue is not any particular chatbot or data center but the companies building them. The coalition comes first; the policy, after, Aroneanu told me. “You have to show the benefits to people immediately. It’s gotta land in their pocketbooks almost immediately for it to have political salience. And then you have to keep defending it.” Opinions about specific aspects of AI may differ, but fundamentally, people don’t like that “this technology is coming into their lives and they have very little control over it,” says Caroline Behringer, a communications strategist who worked on President Obamaʼs Climate Action Plan and now runs Athena Insights, a polling organization that studies attitudes toward AI. The movement, in Aroneanu’s words, must be polarized not left-right, but “down-up.” Of course, Irreplaceable’s climate roots link it to progressive causes, and the group will primarily focus on organizing the center-left around AI. When I asked Aroneanu if he worried this might be counterproductive—polarizing the issue and allowing for the kind of partisan rancor and backsliding that beset climate activism—his response was pragmatic. “Chances are, this issue becomes polarized,” Aroneanu said. “I think that political parties are really exceptionally good at generating negative partisanship,” just as industry is likely to “split the base.” At some point, the climate movement had to decide that the best strategy was to accept partisanship and build power from the left. Although Irreplaceable hopes that conservative counterparts will emerge and believes its populist message will cross culture-war lines, Aroneanu does not see this as his explicit remit. Broad, at times even ambiguous, backlash may make sense if AI is a general-purpose technology, as Silicon Valley is fond of saying—which is to say, if the technology touches and even upends nearly every aspect of the economy. Creating a technical oversight body for AI cyberattacks will not protect every American’s livelihood during mass layoffs; wealth redistribution will not prevent AI companies from spying on your most intimate interactions with a chatbot; voting won’t matter as much if AI companies become more powerful than Congress. Major figures at both OpenAI and Anthropic have suggested that a true AI revolution could require new democratic and economic institutions. Maybe they’re right. And maybe these companies, which have already torn down so much, should not also be the ones in charge of rebuilding.

items.title: OUBRI/IPO 2026 : 2 324 jeunes achèvent leur immersion patriotique
items.description: OUBRI/IPO 2026 : 2 324 jeunes achèvent leur immersion patriotique Ziniaré, 27 août 2026 (AIB)-La deuxième édition de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) a pris fin jeudi à Ziniaré, avec la participation de 2 324 jeunes appelés, au cours d’une cérémonie présidée par le gouverneur de la région de Oubri, Sy Assetou BARRY/TRAORÉ. La cérémonie de clôture s’est tenue sur l’aire du 11-Décembre de Ziniaré, en présence des autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), des appelés et de leurs parents. Les 2 324 appelés étaient répartis sur trois sites : l’Institut national de formation des personnels de l’éducation (INFPE), ex-ENEP de Loumbila, le Service national de développement (SND) de Loumbila et le lycée provincial Bassy de Ziniaré. Au cours de leur immersion, les jeunes ont participé à des activités destinées à renforcer leur patriotisme, leur civisme, leur discipline et leur sens des responsabilités. Ils ont également été sensibilisés sur leurs devoirs envers la Nation et l’importance de l’engagement citoyen. Pour le gouverneur, Sy Assetou BARRY/TRAORÉ, le patriotisme ne doit pas rester un simple concept. « Être patriote, c’est avoir l’amour inconditionnel et un engagement fort pour sa Patrie », a-t-elle déclaré. Elle s’est réjouie de voir une jeunesse déterminée à prolonger les enseignements reçus au-delà des sites d’immersion. « Nous sommes fiers de voir ces appelés, une jeunesse déterminée à faire vivre, au-delà des sites, ce sentiment d’appartenance à la Nation et surtout l’engagement à faire en sorte que le Burkina puisse compter sur eux », a-t-elle souligné. Le gouverneur a invité les jeunes à devenir des modèles dans leurs familles, leurs communautés et leurs structures d’enseignement. « Je leur lance l’appel d’être un modèle partout où ils seront et surtout de garder la flamme de l’engagement à servir leur Nation allumée », a-t-elle ajouté. Claudia KABORE/SOUGUE , parente d’une appelée, a salué l’initiative. Elle a reconnu avoir eu des appréhensions au début, mais estime que l’immersion constitue une opportunité pour les jeunes de mieux connaître leur pays et d’intégrer les valeurs nécessaires à leur épanouissement. De son côté, l’appelé Oumarou KABORE s’est dit fier de son expérience. Selon lui, l’immersion a été un moment d’éducation et d’apprentissage autour de valeurs telles que le patriotisme, l’intégrité, la probité, la solidarité et la tolérance. Il a au nom de toute la promotion remercier le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré . À travers les différentes interventions, les participants ont appelé les jeunes à faire vivre ces valeurs dans leur quotidien et à contribuer, par leur comportement, à la construction et à la défense de la Nation. Agence d'information du Burkina SO/LC
